8718.label: 1 Kings 1:1
8718.text: Now King David was old, advanced in days; and they would cover him with garments, but he would not feel warm.

8719.label: 1 Kings 1:2
8719.text: So his servants said to him: “Let them look for a girl, a virgin, for my lord the king, and she will have to attend upon the king, that she may become his nurse; and she must lie in your bosom, and my lord the king will certainly feel warm.”

8720.label: 1 Kings 1:3
8720.text: And they went looking for a beautiful girl throughout all the territory of Israel, and finally found Abʹi·shag the Shuʹnam·mite and then brought her in to the king.

8721.label: 1 Kings 1:4
8721.text: And the girl was beautiful in the extreme; and she came to be the king’s nurse and kept waiting upon him, and the king himself had no intercourse with her.

8722.label: 1 Kings 1:5
8722.text: All the while Ad·o·niʹjah the son of Hagʹgith was lifting himself up, saying: “I myself am going to rule as king!” And he proceeded to have a chariot made for himself with horsemen and fifty men running before him.

8723.label: 1 Kings 1:6
8723.text: And his father did not hurt his feelings at any time by saying: “Why is this the way you have done?” And he was also very good-looking in form, and [his mother] had borne him after Abʹsa·lom.

8724.label: 1 Kings 1:7
8724.text: And he came to have dealings with Joʹab the son of Ze·ruʹiah and with A·biʹa·thar the priest, and they began offering help as followers of Ad·o·niʹjah.

8725.label: 1 Kings 1:8
8725.text: As for Zaʹdok the priest and Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da and Nathan the prophet and Shimʹe·i and Reʹi and the mighty men that belonged to David, they did not become involved with Ad·o·niʹjah.

8726.label: 1 Kings 1:9
8726.text: Eventually Ad·o·niʹjah held a sacrifice of sheep and cattle and fatlings close by the stone of Zoʹhe·leth, which is beside En-roʹgel, and he proceeded to invite all his brothers the king’s sons and all the men of Judah the king’s servants;

8727.label: 1 Kings 1:10
8727.text: and Nathan the prophet and Be·naiʹah and the mighty men and Solʹo·mon his brother he did not invite.

8728.label: 1 Kings 1:11
8728.text: Nathan now said to Bath-sheʹba, Solʹo·mon’s mother: “Have you not heard that Ad·o·niʹjah the son of Hagʹgith has become king, and our lord David does not know of it at all?

8729.label: 1 Kings 1:12
8729.text: So now come, let me, please, solemnly counsel you. And provide escape for your own soul and for the soul of your son Solʹo·mon.

8730.label: 1 Kings 1:13
8730.text: Go and enter in to King David, and you must say to him, ‘Was it not you, my lord the king, that swore to your slave girl, saying: “Solʹo·mon your son is the one that will become king after me, and he is the one that will sit upon my throne”? So why has Ad·o·niʹjah become king?’

8731.label: 1 Kings 1:14
8731.text: Look! While you are yet speaking there with the king, then I myself shall come in after you, and I shall certainly confirm your words.”

8732.label: 1 Kings 1:15
8732.text: Accordingly Bath-sheʹba went in to the king in the interior room, and the king was very old, and Abʹi·shag the Shuʹnam·mite was waiting upon the king.

8733.label: 1 Kings 1:16
8733.text: Then Bath-sheʹba bowed low and prostrated herself to the king, upon which the king said: “What do you have [to ask]?”

8734.label: 1 Kings 1:17
8734.text: At this she said to him: “My lord, it was you that swore by Jehovah your God to your slave girl, ‘Solʹo·mon your son is the one that will become king after me, and he is the one that will sit upon my throne.’

8735.label: 1 Kings 1:18
8735.text: And now, look! Ad·o·niʹjah himself has become king, and now my lord the king himself does not know of it at all.

8736.label: 1 Kings 1:19
8736.text: So he sacrificed bulls and fatlings and sheep in great quantity and invited all the sons of the king and A·biʹa·thar the priest and Joʹab the chief of the army; but Solʹo·mon your servant he has not invited.

8737.label: 1 Kings 1:20
8737.text: And you my lord the king—the eyes of all Israel are upon you, to tell them who is going to sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him.

8738.label: 1 Kings 1:21
8738.text: And it will certainly occur that as soon as my lord the king lies down with his forefathers, I myself and also my son Solʹo·mon shall certainly become offenders.”

8739.label: 1 Kings 1:22
8739.text: And, look! while she was yet speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet himself came in.

8740.label: 1 Kings 1:23
8740.text: At once they told the king, saying: “Here is Nathan the prophet!” After that he came in before the king and prostrated himself to the king with his face to the earth.

8741.label: 1 Kings 1:24
8741.text: Then Nathan said: “My lord the king, did you yourself say, ‘Ad·o·niʹjah is the one that will become king after me, and he is the one that will sit upon my throne’?

8742.label: 1 Kings 1:25
8742.text: For he has today gone down that he might sacrifice bulls and fatlings and sheep in great quantity and might invite all the sons of the king and the chiefs of the army and A·biʹa·thar the priest; and there they are eating and drinking before him and they keep saying, ‘Let King Ad·o·niʹjah live!’

8743.label: 1 Kings 1:26
8743.text: But as for me your servant, me and Zaʹdok the priest and Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da and Solʹo·mon your servant he has not invited.

8744.label: 1 Kings 1:27
8744.text: If it is from my lord the king that this thing has been brought about, then you have not caused your servant to know who should sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him.”

8745.label: 1 Kings 1:28
8745.text: King David now answered and said: “YOU men, call Bath-sheʹba for me.” At that she came in before the king and stood before the king.

8746.label: 1 Kings 1:29
8746.text: And the king proceeded to swear and say: “As Jehovah is living who redeemed my soul out of all distress,

8747.label: 1 Kings 1:30
8747.text: just as I have sworn to you by Jehovah the God of Israel, saying, ‘Solʹo·mon your son is the one that will become king after me, and he is the one that will sit upon my throne in place of me!’ that is the way I shall do this day.”

8748.label: 1 Kings 1:31
8748.text: Then Bath-sheʹba bowed low with her face to the earth and prostrated herself to the king and said: “Let my lord King David live to time indefinite!”

8749.label: 1 Kings 1:32
8749.text: Immediately King David said: “YOU men, call for me Zaʹdok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da.” So they came in before the king.

8750.label: 1 Kings 1:33
8750.text: And the king went on to say to them: “Take with YOU the servants of YOUR lord, and YOU must make Solʹo·mon my son ride upon the she-mule that belongs to me and lead him down to Giʹhon.

8751.label: 1 Kings 1:34
8751.text: And Zaʹdok the priest and Nathan the prophet must anoint him there as king over Israel; and YOU must blow the horn and say, ‘Let King Solʹo·mon live!’

8752.label: 1 Kings 1:35
8752.text: And YOU must come up following him, and he must come in and sit upon my throne; and he himself will be king in place of me, and him I shall have to commission to become leader over Israel and over Judah.”

8753.label: 1 Kings 1:36
8753.text: At once Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da answered the king and said: “Amen! Thus may Jehovah the God of my lord the king say.

8754.label: 1 Kings 1:37
8754.text: Just as Jehovah proved to be with my lord the king, so let him prove to be with Solʹo·mon, and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.”

8755.label: 1 Kings 1:38
8755.text: And Zaʹdok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da and the Cherʹe·thites and the Pelʹe·thites proceeded to go down and make Solʹo·mon ride upon the she-mule of King David, and then brought him to Giʹhon.

8756.label: 1 Kings 1:39
8756.text: Zaʹdok the priest now took the horn of oil out of the tent and anointed Solʹo·mon; and they began to blow the horn, and all the people broke out saying: “Let King Solʹo·mon live!”

8757.label: 1 Kings 1:40
8757.text: After that all the people came on up following him, and the people were playing on flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth was split by the noise of them.

8758.label: 1 Kings 1:41
8758.text: And Ad·o·niʹjah and all the ones invited that were with him got to hear it, when they themselves had finished eating. When Joʹab got to hear the sound of the horn, he at once said: “What does the noise of the town in an uproar mean?”

8759.label: 1 Kings 1:42
8759.text: While he was yet speaking, why, here Jonʹa·than the son of A·biʹa·thar the priest came. Then Ad·o·niʹjah said: “Come on in, for you are a valiant man, and you bring good news.”

8760.label: 1 Kings 1:43
8760.text: But Jonʹa·than answered and said to Ad·o·niʹjah: “No! Our lord King David himself has made Solʹo·mon king.

8761.label: 1 Kings 1:44
8761.text: So the king sent with him Zaʹdok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da and the Cherʹe·thites and the Pelʹe·thites, and they made him ride upon the she-mule of the king.

8762.label: 1 Kings 1:45
8762.text: Then Zaʹdok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him as king in Giʹhon; after which they came up from there rejoicing, and the town is in an uproar. That was the noise that YOU men heard.

8763.label: 1 Kings 1:46
8763.text: And, besides, Solʹo·mon has sat down upon the throne of the kingship.

8764.label: 1 Kings 1:47
8764.text: And, another thing, the servants of the king have come in to wish our lord King David well, saying, ‘May your God make Solʹo·mon’s name more splendid than your name, and may he make his throne greater than your throne!’ At that the king bowed down upon the bed.

8765.label: 1 Kings 1:48
8765.text: And too this is what the king said, ‘Blessed be Jehovah the God of Israel, who has today given one to sit upon my throne, with my own eyes seeing it!’”

8766.label: 1 Kings 1:49
8766.text: And all those invited that were with Ad·o·niʹjah began to tremble and rise up and go each one on his own way.

8767.label: 1 Kings 1:50
8767.text: And Ad·o·niʹjah himself was afraid because of Solʹo·mon. So he rose up and went away and grabbed hold of the horns of the altar.

8768.label: 1 Kings 1:51
8768.text: In time the report was made to Solʹo·mon, saying: “Here Ad·o·niʹjah himself has become afraid of King Solʹo·mon; and here he has taken hold on the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Solʹo·mon first of all swear to me that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.’”

8769.label: 1 Kings 1:52
8769.text: To this Solʹo·mon said: “If he will become a valiant man, there will not fall a single hair of his to the earth; but if what is bad should be found in him, he will also have to die.”

8770.label: 1 Kings 1:53
8770.text: So King Solʹo·mon sent and they brought him down from off the altar. Then he came in and bowed down to King Solʹo·mon; after which Solʹo·mon said to him: “Go to your own house.”

8771.label: 1 Kings 2:1
8771.text: And the days of David gradually drew near for him to die; and he proceeded to command Solʹo·mon his son, saying:

8772.label: 1 Kings 2:2
8772.text: “I am going in the way of all the earth, and you must be strong and prove yourself to be a man.

8773.label: 1 Kings 2:3
8773.text: And you must keep the obligation to Jehovah your God by walking in his ways, by keeping his statutes, his commandments and his judicial decisions and his testimonies, according to what is written in the law of Moses, in order that you may act prudently in everything that you do and everywhere that you turn;

8774.label: 1 Kings 2:4
8774.text: in order that Jehovah may carry out his word that he spoke respecting me, saying, ‘If your sons will take care of their way by walking before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there will not be cut off a man of yours from [sitting] upon the throne of Israel.’

8775.label: 1 Kings 2:5
8775.text: “And you yourself also well know what Joʹab the son of Ze·ruʹiah did to me in what he did to two chiefs of the armies of Israel, to Abʹner the son of Ner and A·maʹsa the son of Jeʹther, when he killed them and placed the blood of war in peacetime and put the blood of war on his belt that was about his hips and in his sandals that were on his feet.

8776.label: 1 Kings 2:6
8776.text: And you must act according to your wisdom, and not let his gray hairs go down in peace to Sheʹol.

8777.label: 1 Kings 2:7
8777.text: “And toward the sons of Bar·zilʹlai the Gilʹe·ad·ite you should exercise loving-kindness, and they must prove to be among those eating at your table; for that was the way they drew near to me when I ran away from before Abʹsa·lom your brother.

8778.label: 1 Kings 2:8
8778.text: “And here there is with you Shimʹe·i the son of Geʹra the Benʹja·min·ite from Ba·huʹrim, and he it was that called down evil upon me with a painful malediction on the day that I was going to Ma·ha·naʹim; and he it was that came down to meet me at the Jordan, so that I swore to him by Jehovah, saying, ‘I shall not put you to death by the sword.’

8779.label: 1 Kings 2:9
8779.text: And now do not leave him unpunished, for you are a wise man and you well know what you ought to do to him, and you must bring his gray hairs down to Sheʹol with blood.”

8780.label: 1 Kings 2:10
8780.text: Then David lay down with his forefathers and was buried in the City of David.

8781.label: 1 Kings 2:11
8781.text: And the days that David had reigned over Israel were forty years. In Heʹbron he had reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he had reigned thirty-three years.

8782.label: 1 Kings 2:12
8782.text: As for Solʹo·mon, he sat down upon the throne of David his father; and gradually his kingship became very firmly established.

8783.label: 1 Kings 2:13
8783.text: In time Ad·o·niʹjah the son of Hagʹgith came to Bath-sheʹba, Solʹo·mon’s mother. At this she said: “Is your coming peaceable?” to which he said: “It is peaceable.”

8784.label: 1 Kings 2:14
8784.text: And he went on to say: “There is a matter I have for you.” So she said: “Speak.”

8785.label: 1 Kings 2:15
8785.text: And he continued: “You yourself well know that the kingship was to have become mine, and it was toward me that all Israel had set their face for me to become king; but the kingship turned and came to be my brother’s, for it was from Jehovah that it became his.

8786.label: 1 Kings 2:16
8786.text: And now there is one request that I am making of you. Do not turn my face away.” Accordingly she said to him: “Speak.”

8787.label: 1 Kings 2:17
8787.text: And he went on to say: “Please, say to Solʹo·mon the king (for he will not turn your face away) that he should give me Abʹi·shag the Shuʹnam·mite as a wife.”

8788.label: 1 Kings 2:18
8788.text: To this Bath-sheʹba said: “Good! I myself shall speak for you to the king.”

8789.label: 1 Kings 2:19
8789.text: So Bath-sheʹba came in to King Solʹo·mon to speak to him for Ad·o·niʹjah. At once the king rose to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat down upon his throne and had a throne set for the mother of the king, that she might sit at his right.

8790.label: 1 Kings 2:20
8790.text: And she proceeded to say: “There is one little request that I am making of you. Do not turn my face away.” So the king said to her: “Make it, my mother; for I shall not turn your face away.”

8791.label: 1 Kings 2:21
8791.text: And she went on to say: “Let Abʹi·shag the Shuʹnam·mite be given to Ad·o·niʹjah your brother as a wife.”

8792.label: 1 Kings 2:22
8792.text: At this King Solʹo·mon answered and said to his mother: “And why are you requesting Abʹi·shag the Shuʹnam·mite for Ad·o·niʹjah? Request also for him the kingship (because he is my brother older than I am), even for him and for A·biʹa·thar the priest and for Joʹab the son of Ze·ruʹiah.”

8793.label: 1 Kings 2:23
8793.text: With that King Solʹo·mon swore by Jehovah, saying: “So may God do to me, and so may he add to it, if it was not against his own soul that Ad·o·niʹjah spoke this thing.

8794.label: 1 Kings 2:24
8794.text: And now, as Jehovah is living who has firmly established me and keeps me seated upon the throne of David my father and who made a house for me just as he has spoken, today Ad·o·niʹjah will be put to death.”

8795.label: 1 Kings 2:25
8795.text: Immediately King Solʹo·mon sent by means of Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da; and he proceeded to fall upon him, so that he died.

8796.label: 1 Kings 2:26
8796.text: And to A·biʹa·thar the priest the king said: “Go to Anʹa·thoth to your fields! For you are deserving of death; but on this day I shall not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah before David my father, and because you suffered affliction during all the time that my father suffered affliction.”

8797.label: 1 Kings 2:27
8797.text: So Solʹo·mon drove out A·biʹa·thar from serving as a priest of Jehovah, to fulfill Jehovah’s word that he had spoken against the house of Eʹli in Shiʹloh.

8798.label: 1 Kings 2:28
8798.text: And the report itself came clear to Joʹab —for Joʹab himself had inclined to follow Ad·o·niʹjah, although Abʹsa·lom he had not inclined to follow —and Joʹab went fleeing to the tent of Jehovah and began to hold fast to the horns of the altar.

8799.label: 1 Kings 2:29
8799.text: Then King Solʹo·mon was told: “Joʹab has fled to the tent of Jehovah, and there he is beside the altar.” So Solʹo·mon sent Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da, saying: “Go, fall upon him!”

8800.label: 1 Kings 2:30
8800.text: Accordingly Be·naiʹah came to the tent of Jehovah and said to him: “This is what the king has said, ‘Come on out!’” But he said: “No! For here is where I shall die.” At that Be·naiʹah brought word back to the king, saying: “This is what Joʹab spoke, and this is what he answered me.”

8801.label: 1 Kings 2:31
8801.text: Then the king said to him: “Do just as he has spoken and fall upon him; and you must bury him and remove from off me and from off the house of my father the blood undeservedly shed that Joʹab spilled.

8802.label: 1 Kings 2:32
8802.text: And Jehovah will certainly bring back his blood upon his own head, because he fell upon two men more righteous and better than he was, and he proceeded to kill them with the sword, when my father David himself had not known of it, namely, Abʹner the son of Ner the chief of the army of Israel and A·maʹsa the son of Jeʹther the chief of the army of Judah.

8803.label: 1 Kings 2:33
8803.text: And their blood must come back upon the head of Joʹab and upon the head of his offspring to time indefinite; but for David and for his offspring and for his house and for his throne there will come to be peace to time indefinite from Jehovah.”

8804.label: 1 Kings 2:34
8804.text: Then Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da went on up and fell upon him and put him to death; and he got to be buried at his own house in the wilderness.

8805.label: 1 Kings 2:35
8805.text: Upon that the king put Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da in place of him over the army; and Zaʹdok the priest the king put in the place of A·biʹa·thar.

8806.label: 1 Kings 2:36
8806.text: Finally the king sent and called Shimʹe·i and said to him: “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem, and you must dwell there and not go out from there to this place and that.

8807.label: 1 Kings 2:37
8807.text: And it must occur that on the day of your going out and when you do pass over the torrent valley of Kidʹron, you should unmistakably know that you will positively die. Bloodguilt for you will itself come to be upon your own head.”

8808.label: 1 Kings 2:38
8808.text: At this Shimʹe·i said to the king: “The word is good. Just as my lord the king has spoken is the way that your servant will do.” And Shimʹe·i kept dwelling in Jerusalem many days.

8809.label: 1 Kings 2:39
8809.text: And it came about at the end of three years that two slaves of Shimʹe·i went running away to Aʹchish the son of Maʹa·cah the king of Gath; and people came telling Shimʹe·i, saying: “Look! Your slaves are at Gath.”

8810.label: 1 Kings 2:40
8810.text: Immediately Shimʹe·i got up and saddled his ass and went to Gath to Aʹchish to look for his slaves; after which Shimʹe·i went and brought his slaves from Gath.

8811.label: 1 Kings 2:41
8811.text: Then Solʹo·mon was told: “Shimʹe·i has gone out of Jerusalem to Gath and is back.”

8812.label: 1 Kings 2:42
8812.text: At that the king sent and called Shimʹe·i and said to him: “Did I not put you under oath by Jehovah that I might warn you, saying, ‘On the day of your going outside and when you do go here and there you should unmistakably know that you will positively die,’ and so did you not say to me, ‘Good is the word that I have heard’?

8813.label: 1 Kings 2:43
8813.text: Why, then, did you not keep the oath of Jehovah and the commandment that I solemnly laid upon you?”

8814.label: 1 Kings 2:44
8814.text: And the king went on to say to Shimʹe·i: “You yourself certainly know all the injury which your heart well knows that you did to David my father; and Jehovah will certainly return the injury by you upon your own head.

8815.label: 1 Kings 2:45
8815.text: But King Solʹo·mon will be blessed, and the throne of David itself will prove to be firmly established before Jehovah forever.”

8816.label: 1 Kings 2:46
8816.text: With that the king commanded Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da, who then went out and fell upon him, so that he died. And the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solʹo·mon.

8817.label: 1 Kings 3:1
8817.text: And Solʹo·mon proceeded to form a marriage alliance with Pharʹaoh the king of Egypt and to take Pharʹaoh’s daughter and bring her to the City of David, until he finished building his own house and the house of Jehovah and Jerusalem’s wall all around.

8818.label: 1 Kings 3:2
8818.text: Only the people were sacrificing on the high places, for a house had not been built to the name of Jehovah down to those days.

8819.label: 1 Kings 3:3
8819.text: And Solʹo·mon continued to love Jehovah by walking in the statutes of David his father. Only it was on the high places that he was regularly sacrificing and making offerings smoke.

8820.label: 1 Kings 3:4
8820.text: Accordingly the king went to Gibʹe·on to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place. A thousand burnt sacrifices Solʹo·mon proceeded to offer upon that altar.

8821.label: 1 Kings 3:5
8821.text: In Gibʹe·on Jehovah appeared to Solʹo·mon in a dream by night; and God proceeded to say: “Request what I should give you.”

8822.label: 1 Kings 3:6
8822.text: At this Solʹo·mon said: “You yourself have exercised great loving-kindness toward your servant David my father according as he walked before you in truth and in righteousness and in uprightness of heart with you; and you continued keeping toward him this great loving-kindness, so that you gave him a son to sit upon his throne as at this day.

8823.label: 1 Kings 3:7
8823.text: And now, Jehovah my God, you yourself have made your servant king in the place of David my father, and I am but a little boy. I do not know how to go out and how to come in.

8824.label: 1 Kings 3:8
8824.text: And your servant is in the middle of your people whom you have chosen, a multitudinous people that cannot be numbered or counted for multitude.

8825.label: 1 Kings 3:9
8825.text: And you must give to your servant an obedient heart to judge your people, to discern between good and bad; for who is able to judge this difficult people of yours?”

8826.label: 1 Kings 3:10
8826.text: And the thing was pleasing in the eyes of Jehovah, because Solʹo·mon had requested this thing.

8827.label: 1 Kings 3:11
8827.text: And God went on to say to him: “For the reason that you have requested this thing and have not requested for yourself many days nor requested for yourself riches nor requested the soul of your enemies, and you have requested for yourself understanding to hear judicial cases,

8828.label: 1 Kings 3:12
8828.text: look! I shall certainly do according to your words. Look! I shall certainly give you a wise and understanding heart, so that one like you there has not happened to be before you, and after you there will not rise up one like you.

8829.label: 1 Kings 3:13
8829.text: And also what you have not requested I will give you, both riches and glory, so that there will not have happened to be any among the kings like you, all your days.

8830.label: 1 Kings 3:14
8830.text: And if you will walk in my ways by keeping my regulations and my commandments, just as David your father walked, I will also lengthen your days.”

8831.label: 1 Kings 3:15
8831.text: When Solʹo·mon awoke, why, here it had been a dream. Then he came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of Jehovah and offered up burnt sacrifices and rendered up communion offerings and spread a feast for all his servants.

8832.label: 1 Kings 3:16
8832.text: At that time two women, prostitutes, got to come in to the king and stand before him.

8833.label: 1 Kings 3:17
8833.text: Then the one woman said: “Excuse me, my lord, I and this woman are dwelling in one house, so that I gave birth close by her in the house.

8834.label: 1 Kings 3:18
8834.text: And it came about on the third day after I gave birth, this woman also proceeded to give birth. And we were together. There was no stranger with us in the house, no one but the two of us in the house.

8835.label: 1 Kings 3:19
8835.text: Later the son of this woman died at night, because she lay upon him.

8836.label: 1 Kings 3:20
8836.text: So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your slave girl herself was asleep and laid him in her own bosom, and her dead son she laid in my bosom.

8837.label: 1 Kings 3:21
8837.text: When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, why, there he was dead. So I examined him closely in the morning, and, look! he did not prove to be my son that I had borne.”

8838.label: 1 Kings 3:22
8838.text: But the other woman said: “No, but my son is the living one and your son is the dead one!” All the while this woman was saying: “No, but your son is the dead one and my son is the living one.” And they kept on speaking before the king.

8839.label: 1 Kings 3:23
8839.text: Finally the king said: “This one is saying, ‘This is my son, the living one, and your son is the dead one!’ and that one is saying, ‘No, but your son is the dead one and my son is the living one!’”

8840.label: 1 Kings 3:24
8840.text: And the king went on to say: “YOU men, get me a sword.” So they brought the sword before the king.

8841.label: 1 Kings 3:25
8841.text: And the king proceeded to say: “YOU men, sever the living child in two and give the one half to the one woman and the other half to the other.”

8842.label: 1 Kings 3:26
8842.text: At once the woman whose son was the living one said to the king (for her inward emotions were excited toward her son, so that she said): “Excuse me, my lord! YOU men, give her the living child. Do not by any means put him to death.” All the while this other woman was saying: “Neither mine nor yours will he become. YOU men, do the severing!”

8843.label: 1 Kings 3:27
8843.text: At that the king answered and said: “YOU men, give her the living child, and YOU must by no means put him to death. She is his mother.”

8844.label: 1 Kings 3:28
8844.text: And all Israel got to hear of the judicial decision that the king had handed down; and they became fearful because of the king, for they saw that the wisdom of God was within him to execute judicial decision.

8845.label: 1 Kings 4:1
8845.text: And King Solʹo·mon continued king over all Israel.

8846.label: 1 Kings 4:2
8846.text: And these are the princes that he had: Az·a·riʹah the son of Zaʹdok, the priest;

8847.label: 1 Kings 4:3
8847.text: El·i·horʹeph and A·hiʹjah, the sons of Shiʹsha, secretaries; Je·hoshʹa·phat the son of A·hiʹlud, the recorder;

8848.label: 1 Kings 4:4
8848.text: and Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da was over the army, and Zaʹdok and A·biʹa·thar were priests;

8849.label: 1 Kings 4:5
8849.text: and Az·a·riʹah the son of Nathan was over the deputies, and Zaʹbud the son of Nathan was a priest, the friend of the king;

8850.label: 1 Kings 4:6
8850.text: and A·hiʹshar was over the household, and Ad·o·niʹram the son of Abʹda, over those conscripted for forced labor.

8851.label: 1 Kings 4:7
8851.text: And Solʹo·mon had twelve deputies over all Israel, and they provided the king and his household with food. It would devolve upon each one to provide the food one month in the year.

8852.label: 1 Kings 4:8
8852.text: And these were their names: The son of Hur, in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im;

8853.label: 1 Kings 4:9
8853.text: the son of Deʹker, in Maʹkaz and in Sha·alʹbim and Beth-sheʹmesh and Eʹlon-beth-haʹnan;

8854.label: 1 Kings 4:10
8854.text: the son of Heʹsed, in A·rubʹboth (he had Soʹcoh and all the land of Heʹpher);

8855.label: 1 Kings 4:11
8855.text: the son of A·binʹa·dab, all the mountain ridge of Dor (Taʹphath, Solʹo·mon’s daughter, herself became his wife);

8856.label: 1 Kings 4:12
8856.text: Baʹa·na the son of A·hiʹlud, in Taʹa·nach and Me·gidʹdo and all Beth-sheʹan, which is beside Zarʹe·than below Jezʹre·el, from Beth-sheʹan to Aʹbel-me·hoʹlah to the region of Jokʹme·am;

8857.label: 1 Kings 4:13
8857.text: the son of Geʹber, in Raʹmoth-gilʹe·ad (he had the tent villages of Jaʹir the son of Ma·nasʹseh, which are in Gilʹe·ad; he had the region of Arʹgob, which is in Baʹshan: sixty large cities with wall and copper bar);

8858.label: 1 Kings 4:14
8858.text: A·hinʹa·dab the son of Idʹdo, in Ma·ha·naʹim;

8859.label: 1 Kings 4:15
8859.text: A·himʹa·az, in Naphʹta·li (he, too, took Basʹe·math, Solʹo·mon’s daughter, as a wife);

8860.label: 1 Kings 4:16
8860.text: Baʹa·na the son of Huʹshai, in Ashʹer and Be·aʹloth;

8861.label: 1 Kings 4:17
8861.text: Je·hoshʹa·phat the son of Pa·ruʹah, in Isʹsa·char;

8862.label: 1 Kings 4:18
8862.text: Shimʹe·i the son of Eʹla, in Benjamin;

8863.label: 1 Kings 4:19
8863.text: Geʹber the son of Uʹri, in the land of Gilʹe·ad, the land of Siʹhon the king of the Amʹor·ites, and of Og the king of Baʹshan, and there was one deputy [over all the other deputies] that were in the land.

8864.label: 1 Kings 4:20
8864.text: Judah and Israel were many, like the grains of sand that are by the sea for multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing.

8865.label: 1 Kings 4:21
8865.text: As for Solʹo·mon, he proved to be ruler over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Phi·lisʹtines and to the boundary of Egypt. They were bringing gifts and serving Solʹo·mon all the days of his life.

8866.label: 1 Kings 4:22
8866.text: And Solʹo·mon’s food for each day regularly proved to be thirty cor measures of fine flour and sixty cor measures of flour,

8867.label: 1 Kings 4:23
8867.text: ten fat cattle and twenty pastured cattle and a hundred sheep, besides some stags and gazelles and roebucks and fattened cuckoos.

8868.label: 1 Kings 4:24
8868.text: For he was holding in subjection everything this side of the River, from Tiphʹsah to Gaʹza, even all the kings this side of the River; and peace itself became his in every region of his, all around.

8869.label: 1 Kings 4:25
8869.text: And Judah and Israel continued to dwell in security, everyone under his own vine and under his own fig tree, from Dan to Beʹer-sheʹba, all the days of Solʹo·mon.

8870.label: 1 Kings 4:26
8870.text: And Solʹo·mon came to have forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.

8871.label: 1 Kings 4:27
8871.text: And these deputies supplied food to King Solʹo·mon and everyone approaching the table of King Solʹo·mon, each one in his month. They left nothing lacking.

8872.label: 1 Kings 4:28
8872.text: And the barley and the straw for the horses and for the teams of horses they kept bringing to wherever the place might prove to be, each one according to his commission.

8873.label: 1 Kings 4:29
8873.text: And God continued giving Solʹo·mon wisdom and understanding in very great measure and a broadness of heart, like the sand that is upon the seashore.

8874.label: 1 Kings 4:30
8874.text: And Solʹo·mon’s wisdom was vaster than the wisdom of all the Orientals and than all the wisdom of Egypt.

8875.label: 1 Kings 4:31
8875.text: And he was wiser than any other man, than Eʹthan the Ezʹra·hite and Heʹman and Calʹcol and Darʹda the sons of Maʹhol; and his fame came to be in all the nations all around.

8876.label: 1 Kings 4:32
8876.text: And he could speak three thousand proverbs, and his songs came to be a thousand and five.

8877.label: 1 Kings 4:33
8877.text: And he would speak about the trees, from the cedar that is in Lebʹa·non to the hyssop that is coming forth on the wall; and he would speak about the beasts and about the flying creatures and about the moving things and about the fishes.

8878.label: 1 Kings 4:34
8878.text: And they kept coming from all the peoples to hear Solʹo·mon’s wisdom, even from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

8879.label: 1 Kings 5:1
8879.text: And Hiʹram the king of Tyre proceeded to send his servants to Solʹo·mon, for he had heard that it was he that they had anointed as king in place of his father; for a lover of David Hiʹram had always proved to be.

8880.label: 1 Kings 5:2
8880.text: In turn Solʹo·mon sent to Hiʹram, saying:

8881.label: 1 Kings 5:3
8881.text: “You yourself well know that David my father was not able to build a house to the name of Jehovah his God because of the warfare with which they surrounded him, until Jehovah put them under the soles of his feet.

8882.label: 1 Kings 5:4
8882.text: And now Jehovah my God has given me rest all around. There is no resister, and there is nothing bad happening.

8883.label: 1 Kings 5:5
8883.text: And here I am thinking of building a house to the name of Jehovah my God, just as Jehovah promised to David my father, saying, ‘Your son whom I shall put upon your throne in place of you, he is the one that will build the house to my name.’

8884.label: 1 Kings 5:6
8884.text: And now command that they cut for me cedars from Lebʹa·non; and my servants themselves will prove to be with your servants, and the wages of your servants I shall give to you according to all that you may say, for you yourself well know that there is among us no one knowing how to cut trees like the Si·doʹni·ans.”

8885.label: 1 Kings 5:7
8885.text: And it came about that as soon as Hiʹram heard the words of Solʹo·mon, he began to rejoice greatly, and he went on to say: “Blessed is Jehovah today in that he has given David a wise son over this numerous people!”

8886.label: 1 Kings 5:8
8886.text: Accordingly Hiʹram sent to Solʹo·mon, saying: “I have heard what you sent to me. For my part, I shall do all your delight in the matter of timbers of cedar trees and timbers of juniper trees.

8887.label: 1 Kings 5:9
8887.text: My servants themselves will bring them down out of Lebʹa·non to the sea; and I, for my part, shall put them in log rafts [to go] by sea clear to the place that you will send me notice of; and I shall certainly have them broken up there, and you, for your part, will carry them; and you, for your part, will do my delight by giving the food for my household.”

8888.label: 1 Kings 5:10
8888.text: So Hiʹram became a giver of timbers of cedar trees and timbers of juniper trees to Solʹo·mon according to all his delight.

8889.label: 1 Kings 5:11
8889.text: And Solʹo·mon, for his part, gave Hiʹram twenty thousand cor measures of wheat as food supplies for his household and twenty cor measures of beaten-out oil. That was what Solʹo·mon kept giving Hiʹram year by year.

8890.label: 1 Kings 5:12
8890.text: And Jehovah, for his part, gave Solʹo·mon wisdom, just as he had promised him; and there came to be peace between Hiʹram and Solʹo·mon, and both of them proceeded to conclude a covenant.

8891.label: 1 Kings 5:13
8891.text: And King Solʹo·mon kept bringing up those conscripted for forced labor out of all Israel; and those conscripted for forced labor amounted to thirty thousand men.

8892.label: 1 Kings 5:14
8892.text: And he would send them to Lebʹa·non in shifts of ten thousand a month. For a month they would continue in Lebʹa·non, for two months at their homes; and Ad·o·niʹram was over those conscripted for forced labor.

8893.label: 1 Kings 5:15
8893.text: And Solʹo·mon came to have seventy thousand burden bearers and eighty thousand cutters in the mountain,

8894.label: 1 Kings 5:16
8894.text: besides Solʹo·mon’s princely deputies who were over the work, three thousand three hundred foremen over the people who were active in the work.

8895.label: 1 Kings 5:17
8895.text: Accordingly the king commanded that they should quarry great stones, expensive stones, to lay the foundation of the house with hewn stones.

8896.label: 1 Kings 5:18
8896.text: So Solʹo·mon’s builders and Hiʹram’s builders and the Geʹbal·ites did the cutting, and they kept preparing the timbers and the stones to build the house.

8897.label: 1 Kings 6:1
8897.text: And it came about in the four hundred and eightieth year after the sons of Israel came out from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv, that is, the second month, after Solʹo·mon became king over Israel, that he proceeded to build the house to Jehovah.

8898.label: 1 Kings 6:2
8898.text: And the house that King Solʹo·mon built to Jehovah was sixty cubits in its length, and twenty in its width, and thirty cubits in its height.

8899.label: 1 Kings 6:3
8899.text: And the porch in front of the temple of the house was twenty cubits in its length, in front of the width of the house. Ten cubits it was in its depth, in front of the house.

8900.label: 1 Kings 6:4
8900.text: And for the house he went on to make windows of narrowing frames.

8901.label: 1 Kings 6:5
8901.text: Further, he built against the wall of the house a side structure all around, [against] the walls of the house all around the temple and the innermost room, and made side chambers all around.

8902.label: 1 Kings 6:6
8902.text: The lowest side chamber was five cubits in its width, and the middle one was six cubits in its width, and the third one was seven cubits in its width; for there were cutbacks that he gave to the house all around outside, that it might not have a hold in the walls of the house.

8903.label: 1 Kings 6:7
8903.text: As for the house, while it was being built, it was of quarry stone already completed that it was built; and as for hammers and axes or any tools of iron, they were not heard in the house while it was being built.

8904.label: 1 Kings 6:8
8904.text: The entrance of the lowest side chamber was on the right side of the house, and by a winding staircase they would go up to the middle one, and from the middle one up to the third one.

8905.label: 1 Kings 6:9
8905.text: Further, he continued building the house that he might finish it, and covered in the house with beams and rows in cedarwood.

8906.label: 1 Kings 6:10
8906.text: Moreover, he built the side chambers against the whole house five cubits in their height, and they had a hold on the house by timbers of cedar trees.

8907.label: 1 Kings 6:11
8907.text: Meantime, the word of Jehovah came to Solʹo·mon, saying:

8908.label: 1 Kings 6:12
8908.text: “As regards this house that you are building, if you will walk in my statutes and perform my judicial decisions and actually keep all my commandments by walking in them, I also shall certainly carry out my word with you that I spoke to David your father;

8909.label: 1 Kings 6:13
8909.text: and I shall indeed reside in the middle of the sons of Israel, and I shall not leave my people Israel.”

8910.label: 1 Kings 6:14
8910.text: And Solʹo·mon continued building the house that he might finish it.

8911.label: 1 Kings 6:15
8911.text: And he proceeded to build the walls of the house inside it with boards of cedar. From the floor of the house up to the rafters of the ceiling he overlaid it with timber inside; and he went on to overlay the floor of the house with boards of juniper.

8912.label: 1 Kings 6:16
8912.text: Further, he built twenty cubits at the rear sides of the house with boards of cedar, from the floor up to the rafters, and built for it inside the innermost room, the Most Holy.

8913.label: 1 Kings 6:17
8913.text: And it was forty cubits that the house proved to be, that is, the temple in front of it.

8914.label: 1 Kings 6:18
8914.text: And [the] cedarwood on the house inside was with carvings of gourd-shaped ornaments and garlands of blossoms. All of it was cedarwood; there was no stone to be seen.

8915.label: 1 Kings 6:19
8915.text: And the innermost room in the interior of the house he prepared inside, to put there the ark of the covenant of Jehovah.

8916.label: 1 Kings 6:20
8916.text: And the innermost room was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height; and he proceeded to overlay it with pure gold, and to overlay the altar with cedarwood.

8917.label: 1 Kings 6:21
8917.text: And Solʹo·mon went on to overlay the house inside with pure gold, and to make chainwork of gold pass across in front of the innermost room, and to overlay it with gold.

8918.label: 1 Kings 6:22
8918.text: And the whole house he overlaid with gold, until all the house was completed; and all the altar that was toward the innermost room he overlaid with gold.

8919.label: 1 Kings 6:23
8919.text: Further, he made in the innermost room two cherubs of oil-tree wood, ten cubits being the height of each one.

8920.label: 1 Kings 6:24
8920.text: And five cubits was the one wing of the cherub, and five cubits was the other wing of the cherub. Ten cubits it was from the tip of his wing to the tip of his wing.

8921.label: 1 Kings 6:25
8921.text: And the second cherub was ten cubits. The two cherubs had the same measure and the same shape.

8922.label: 1 Kings 6:26
8922.text: The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and that was so of the other cherub.

8923.label: 1 Kings 6:27
8923.text: Then he put the cherubs inside the inner house, so that they spread out the wings of the cherubs. Thus the wing of the one reached to the wall and the wing of the other cherub was reaching to the other wall; and their wings were toward the middle of the house, reaching wing to wing.

8924.label: 1 Kings 6:28
8924.text: Moreover, he overlaid the cherubs with gold.

8925.label: 1 Kings 6:29
8925.text: And all the walls of the house round about he carved with engraved carvings of cherubs and palm-tree figures and engravings of blossoms, inside and outside;

8926.label: 1 Kings 6:30
8926.text: and the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, inside and outside.

8927.label: 1 Kings 6:31
8927.text: And the entrance of the innermost room he made with doors of oil-tree wood: side pillars, doorposts [and] a fifth.

8928.label: 1 Kings 6:32
8928.text: And the two doors were of oil-tree wood, and he carved upon them carvings of cherubs and palm-tree figures and the engravings of blossoms, and he overlaid them with gold; and he proceeded to beat the gold down upon the cherubs and the palm-tree figures.

8929.label: 1 Kings 6:33
8929.text: And that was the way he made for the entrance of the temple, the doorposts of oil-tree wood, foursquare.

8930.label: 1 Kings 6:34
8930.text: And the two doors were of juniper wood. The two leaves of the one door turned on pivots, and the two leaves of the other door turned on pivots.

8931.label: 1 Kings 6:35
8931.text: And he carved cherubs and palm-tree figures and engravings of blossoms, and overlaid gold foil upon the representations.

8932.label: 1 Kings 6:36
8932.text: And he went on to build the inner courtyard with three rows of hewn stone and a row of beams of cedarwood.

8933.label: 1 Kings 6:37
8933.text: In the fourth year the house of Jehovah had its foundation laid, in the lunar month of Ziv;

8934.label: 1 Kings 6:38
8934.text: and in the eleventh year, in the lunar month of Bul, that is, the eighth month, the house was finished as regards all its details and all its plan; so that he was seven years at building it.

8935.label: 1 Kings 7:1
8935.text: And his own house Solʹo·mon built in thirteen years, so that he finished all his own house.

8936.label: 1 Kings 7:2
8936.text: And he proceeded to build the House of the Forest of Lebʹa·non a hundred cubits in its length, and fifty cubits in its width, and thirty cubits in its height, upon four rows of pillars of cedarwood; and there were beams of cedarwood upon the pillars.

8937.label: 1 Kings 7:3
8937.text: And it was paneled in with cedarwood above upon the girders that were upon the forty-five pillars. There were fifteen to a row.

8938.label: 1 Kings 7:4
8938.text: As for framed windows, there were three rows, and there was an illumination opening opposite an illumination opening in three tiers.

8939.label: 1 Kings 7:5
8939.text: And all the entrances and the doorposts were squared [with the] frame, and also the forefront of the illumination opening opposite an illumination opening in three tiers.

8940.label: 1 Kings 7:6
8940.text: And the Porch of Pillars he made fifty cubits in its length, and thirty cubits in its width; and another porch was in front of them with pillars and a canopy in front of them.

8941.label: 1 Kings 7:7
8941.text: As for the Porch of the Throne where he would do judging, he made the porch of judgment; and they covered it in with cedarwood from the floor to the rafters.

8942.label: 1 Kings 7:8
8942.text: As regards the house of his where he was to dwell, at the other courtyard, it was away from the house belonging to the Porch. It proved to be like this in workmanship. And there was a house like this Porch that he proceeded to build for Pharʹaoh’s daughter, whom Solʹo·mon had taken.

8943.label: 1 Kings 7:9
8943.text: All these were [of] expensive stones according to measures, hewn, sawed with stone-saws, inside and outside, and from the foundation up to the coping, and outside as far as the great courtyard.

8944.label: 1 Kings 7:10
8944.text: And the expensive stones laid as a foundation were great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.

8945.label: 1 Kings 7:11
8945.text: And up above there were expensive stones according to measures, hewn, and also cedarwood.

8946.label: 1 Kings 7:12
8946.text: As for the great courtyard, round about were three rows of hewn stone and a row of beams of cedarwood; and [this] also for the inner courtyard of the house of Jehovah, and for the porch of the house.

8947.label: 1 Kings 7:13
8947.text: And King Solʹo·mon proceeded to send and fetch Hiʹram out of Tyre.

8948.label: 1 Kings 7:14
8948.text: He was the son of a widowed woman from the tribe of Naphʹta·li, and his father was a Tyrʹi·an man, a worker in copper; and he was full of the wisdom and the understanding and the knowledge for doing every sort of work in copper. Accordingly he came to King Solʹo·mon and began to do all his work.

8949.label: 1 Kings 7:15
8949.text: Then he cast the two pillars of copper, eighteen cubits being the height of each pillar, and a string of twelve cubits would measure around each of the two pillars.

8950.label: 1 Kings 7:16
8950.text: And two capitals he made to put upon the tops of the pillars, cast in copper. Five cubits was the height of the one capital, and five cubits was the height of the other capital.

8951.label: 1 Kings 7:17
8951.text: There were nets in network, twisted ornaments in chainwork, for the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars; seven for the one capital, and seven for the other capital.

8952.label: 1 Kings 7:18
8952.text: And he went on to make the pomegranates and two rows round about upon the one network to cover the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars; and that was what he did for the other capital.

8953.label: 1 Kings 7:19
8953.text: And the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars at the porch were of lily work, of four cubits.

8954.label: 1 Kings 7:20
8954.text: And the capitals were upon the two pillars, also up close beside the belly that was adjoining the network; and there were two hundred pomegranates in rows all around upon each capital.

8955.label: 1 Kings 7:21
8955.text: And he proceeded to set up the pillars belonging to the porch of the temple. So he set up the right-hand pillar and called its name Jaʹchin, and then set up the left-hand pillar and called its name Boʹaz.

8956.label: 1 Kings 7:22
8956.text: And upon the top of the pillars there was lily work. And the work of the pillars was gradually completed.

8957.label: 1 Kings 7:23
8957.text: And he proceeded to make the molten sea ten cubits from its one brim to its other brim, circular all around; and its height was five cubits, and it took a line of thirty cubits to circle all around it.

8958.label: 1 Kings 7:24
8958.text: And there were gourd-shaped ornaments down below its brim all around, encircling it, ten in a cubit, enclosing the sea all around, with two rows of the gourd-shaped ornaments cast in its casting.

8959.label: 1 Kings 7:25
8959.text: It was standing upon twelve bulls, three facing north, and three facing west, and three facing south, and three facing east; and the sea was above upon them, and all their hind parts were toward the center.

8960.label: 1 Kings 7:26
8960.text: And its thickness was a handbreadth; and its brim was like the workmanship of the brim of a cup, a lily blossom. Two thousand bath measures were what it would contain.

8961.label: 1 Kings 7:27
8961.text: And he went on to make the ten carriages of copper, four cubits being the length of each carriage, and four cubits its width, and three cubits its height.

8962.label: 1 Kings 7:28
8962.text: And this was the workmanship of the carriages: they had sidewalls, and the sidewalls were between the crossbars.

8963.label: 1 Kings 7:29
8963.text: And upon the sidewalls that were between the crossbars there were lions, bulls and cherubs, and over the crossbars it was like that. Up above and beneath the lions and the bulls there were wreaths in hanging work.

8964.label: 1 Kings 7:30
8964.text: And there were four wheels of copper to each carriage, with axles of copper; and its four cornerpieces were supports for them. Beneath the basin were the supports, cast with wreaths across from each.

8965.label: 1 Kings 7:31
8965.text: And its mouth from inside to the supports and upward was [?] cubits; and its mouth was round, the workmanship of a stand of one and a half cubits, and also upon its mouth there were carvings. And their sidewalls were squared, not round.

8966.label: 1 Kings 7:32
8966.text: And the four wheels were down below the sidewalls, and the supports of the wheels were by the carriage; and the height of each wheel was one and a half cubits.

8967.label: 1 Kings 7:33
8967.text: And the workmanship of the wheels was like the workmanship of a chariot wheel. Their supports and their felloes and their spokes and their hubs, they were all cast.

8968.label: 1 Kings 7:34
8968.text: And there were four supports upon the four corners of each carriage; its supports were of one piece with the carriage.

8969.label: 1 Kings 7:35
8969.text: And on top of the carriage there was [a stand] a half a cubit in height, circular all around; and upon the top of the carriage its sides and its sidewalls were of one piece with it.

8970.label: 1 Kings 7:36
8970.text: Further, he engraved upon the plates of its sides and upon its sidewalls cherubs, lions and palm-tree figures according to the clear space of each, and wreaths all around.

8971.label: 1 Kings 7:37
8971.text: It was like this that he made the ten carriages; they all had one cast, one measure, one shape.

8972.label: 1 Kings 7:38
8972.text: And he proceeded to make ten basins of copper. Forty bath measures were what each basin would contain. Each basin was four cubits. There was one basin upon each carriage for the ten carriages.

8973.label: 1 Kings 7:39
8973.text: Then he put five carriages on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house; and the sea itself he put to the right side of the house eastward, toward the south.

8974.label: 1 Kings 7:40
8974.text: And Hiʹram gradually made the basins and the shovels and the bowls. At length Hiʹram finished doing all the work that he did for King Solʹo·mon as respects the house of Jehovah:

8975.label: 1 Kings 7:41
8975.text: The two pillars and the bowl-shaped capitals that were upon the top of the two pillars, and the two networks to cover the two round capitals that were upon the top of the pillars,

8976.label: 1 Kings 7:42
8976.text: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates to each network, to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals that were upon the two pillars;

8977.label: 1 Kings 7:43
8977.text: and the ten carriages and the ten basins upon the carriages,

8978.label: 1 Kings 7:44
8978.text: and the one sea and the twelve bulls beneath the sea;

8979.label: 1 Kings 7:45
8979.text: and the cans and the shovels and the bowls and all these utensils, which Hiʹram made of polished copper for King Solʹo·mon for the house of Jehovah.

8980.label: 1 Kings 7:46
8980.text: In the District of the Jordan it was that the king cast them in the clay mold, between Sucʹcoth and Zarʹe·than.

8981.label: 1 Kings 7:47
8981.text: And Solʹo·mon left all the utensils [unweighed] because of so extraordinarily great a quantity. The weight of the copper was not ascertained.

8982.label: 1 Kings 7:48
8982.text: And Solʹo·mon gradually made all the utensils that pertained to the house of Jehovah, the altar of gold and the table on which was the showbread, of gold,

8983.label: 1 Kings 7:49
8983.text: and the lampstands, five to the right and five to the left before the innermost room, of pure gold, and the blossoms and the lamps and the snuffers, of gold,

8984.label: 1 Kings 7:50
8984.text: and the basins and the extinguishers and the bowls and the cups and the fire holders, of pure gold, and the sockets for the doors of the inner house, that is, the Most Holy, and for the doors of the house of the temple, of gold.

8985.label: 1 Kings 7:51
8985.text: Finally all the work that King Solʹo·mon had to do as regards the house of Jehovah was at its completion; and Solʹo·mon began to bring in the things made holy by David his father; the silver and the gold and the articles he put in the treasures of the house of Jehovah.

8986.label: 1 Kings 8:1
8986.text: At that time Solʹo·mon proceeded to congregate the older men of Israel, all the heads of the tribes, the chieftains of the fathers, of the sons of Israel, to King Solʹo·mon at Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of the City of David, that is to say, Zion.

8987.label: 1 Kings 8:2
8987.text: So all the men of Israel congregated themselves to King Solʹo·mon in the lunar month of Ethʹa·nim in the festival, that is, the seventh month.

8988.label: 1 Kings 8:3
8988.text: So all the older men of Israel came, and the priests began to carry the Ark.

8989.label: 1 Kings 8:4
8989.text: And they came bringing up the ark of Jehovah and the tent of meeting and all the holy utensils that were in the tent; and the priests and the Levites came bringing them up.

8990.label: 1 Kings 8:5
8990.text: And King Solʹo·mon and with him all the assembly of Israel, those keeping their appointment with him, were before the Ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for multitude.

8991.label: 1 Kings 8:6
8991.text: Then the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of Jehovah to its place, to the innermost room of the house, the Most Holy, to underneath the wings of the cherubs.

8992.label: 1 Kings 8:7
8992.text: For the cherubs were spreading out their wings over the place of the Ark, so that the cherubs kept the Ark and its poles screened over from above.

8993.label: 1 Kings 8:8
8993.text: But the poles proved to be long, so that the tips of the poles were visible from the Holy in front of the innermost room, but they were not visible outside. And there they continue down to this day.

8994.label: 1 Kings 8:9
8994.text: There was nothing in the Ark but the two stone tablets which Moses had deposited there in Hoʹreb, when Jehovah had covenanted with the sons of Israel while they were coming out from the land of Egypt.

8995.label: 1 Kings 8:10
8995.text: And it came about that when the priests came out from the holy place, the cloud itself filled the house of Jehovah.

8996.label: 1 Kings 8:11
8996.text: And the priests were unable to stand to do their ministering because of the cloud, for the glory of Jehovah filled the house of Jehovah.

8997.label: 1 Kings 8:12
8997.text: At that time Solʹo·mon said: “Jehovah himself said he was to reside in the thick gloom.

8998.label: 1 Kings 8:13
8998.text: I have successfully built a house of lofty abode for you, an established place for you to dwell in to time indefinite.”

8999.label: 1 Kings 8:14
8999.text: Then the king turned his face and began to bless all the congregation of Israel, while all the congregation of Israel were standing up.

9000.label: 1 Kings 8:15
9000.text: And he went on to say: “Blessed is Jehovah the God of Israel, who spoke by his own mouth with David my father, and by his own hand has given fulfillment, saying,

9001.label: 1 Kings 8:16
9001.text: ‘From the day that I brought my people Israel out from Egypt I have not chosen a city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house for my name to continue there; but I shall choose David to come to be over my people Israel.’

9002.label: 1 Kings 8:17
9002.text: And it came to be close to the heart of David my father to build a house to the name of Jehovah the God of Israel.

9003.label: 1 Kings 8:18
9003.text: But Jehovah said to David my father, ‘For the reason that it proved to be close to your heart to build a house to my name, you did well, because it proved to be close to your heart.

9004.label: 1 Kings 8:19
9004.text: Only you yourself will not build the house, but your son who is coming forth from your loins is the one that will build the house to my name.’

9005.label: 1 Kings 8:20
9005.text: And Jehovah proceeded to carry out his word that he had spoken, that I might rise up in the place of David my father and sit upon the throne of Israel, just as Jehovah had spoken, and that I might build the house to the name of Jehovah the God of Israel,

9006.label: 1 Kings 8:21
9006.text: and that I might locate a place there for the Ark where the covenant of Jehovah is that he concluded with our forefathers when he was bringing them out from the land of Egypt.”

9007.label: 1 Kings 8:22
9007.text: And Solʹo·mon began standing before the altar of Jehovah in front of all the congregation of Israel, and he now spread his palms out to the heavens;

9008.label: 1 Kings 8:23
9008.text: and he went on to say: “O Jehovah the God of Israel, there is no God like you in the heavens above or on the earth beneath, keeping the covenant and the loving-kindness toward your servants who are walking before you with all their heart,

9009.label: 1 Kings 8:24
9009.text: you who have kept toward your servant David my father that which you promised him, so that you made the promise with your own mouth, and with your own hand you have made the fulfillment, as at this day.

9010.label: 1 Kings 8:25
9010.text: And now, O Jehovah the God of Israel, keep toward your servant David my father that which you promised him, saying, ‘There will not be cut off a man of yours from before me to sit upon the throne of Israel, if only your sons will take care of their way by walking before me just as you have walked before me.’

9011.label: 1 Kings 8:26
9011.text: And now, O God of Israel, let your promise that you have promised to your servant David my father prove trustworthy, please.

9012.label: 1 Kings 8:27
9012.text: “But will God truly dwell upon the earth? Look! The heavens, yes, the heaven of the heavens, themselves cannot contain you; how much less, then, this house that I have built!

9013.label: 1 Kings 8:28
9013.text: And you must turn toward the prayer of your servant and to his request for favor, O Jehovah my God, to listen to the entreating cry and to the prayer with which your servant is praying before you today;

9014.label: 1 Kings 8:29
9014.text: that your eyes may prove to be opened toward this house night and day, toward the place of which you said, ‘My name will prove to be there,’ to listen to the prayer with which your servant prays toward this place.

9015.label: 1 Kings 8:30
9015.text: And you must listen to the request for favor on the part of your servant and of your people Israel with which they pray toward this place; and may you yourself hear at the place of your dwelling, in the heavens, and you must hear and forgive.

9016.label: 1 Kings 8:31
9016.text: “When a man sins against his fellowman, and he actually lays a cursing upon him to bring him under liability to the curse, and he actually comes [within] the curse before your altar in this house,

9017.label: 1 Kings 8:32
9017.text: then may you yourself hear from the heavens, and you must act and judge your servants by pronouncing the wicked one wicked by putting his way upon his own head, and by pronouncing the righteous one righteous by giving to him according to his own righteousness.

9018.label: 1 Kings 8:33
9018.text: “When your people Israel are defeated before the enemy, because they kept sinning against you, and they indeed return to you and laud your name and pray and make request for favor toward you in this house,

9019.label: 1 Kings 8:34
9019.text: then may you yourself hear from heaven, and you must forgive the sin of your people Israel and you must bring them back to the ground that you gave to their forefathers.

9020.label: 1 Kings 8:35
9020.text: “When heaven is shut up so that no rain occurs, because they kept sinning against you, and they actually pray toward this place and laud your name, and from their sin they turn back, because you kept afflicting them,

9021.label: 1 Kings 8:36
9021.text: then may you yourself hear from the heavens, and you must forgive the sin of your servants, even of your people Israel, because you teach them the good way in which they should walk; and you must give rain upon your land that you have given to your people as a hereditary possession.

9022.label: 1 Kings 8:37
9022.text: “In case a famine occurs in the land, in case a pestilence occurs, in case scorching, mildew, locusts, cockroaches occur; in case their enemy besieges them in the land of their gates —any sort of plague, any sort of malady—

9023.label: 1 Kings 8:38
9023.text: whatever prayer, whatever request for favor there may occur on the part of any man [or] of all your people Israel, because they know each one the plague of his own heart, and they actually spread out their palms to this house,

9024.label: 1 Kings 8:39
9024.text: then may you yourself hear from the heavens, your established place of dwelling, and you must forgive and act and give to each one according to all his ways, because you know his heart (for you yourself alone well know the heart of all the sons of mankind );

9025.label: 1 Kings 8:40
9025.text: to the end that they may fear you all the days that they are alive upon the surface of the ground that you gave to our forefathers.

9026.label: 1 Kings 8:41
9026.text: “And also to the foreigner, who is no part of your people Israel and who actually comes from a distant land by reason of your name

9027.label: 1 Kings 8:42
9027.text: (for they shall hear of your great name and of your strong hand and of your stretched-out arm), and he actually comes and prays toward this house,

9028.label: 1 Kings 8:43
9028.text: may you yourself listen from the heavens, your established place of dwelling, and you must do according to all that for which the foreigner calls to you; in order that all the peoples of the earth may get to know your name so as to fear you the same as your people Israel do, and so as to know that your name itself has been called upon this house that I have built.

9029.label: 1 Kings 8:44
9029.text: “In case your people go out to the war against their enemy in the way that you send them, and they indeed pray to Jehovah in the direction of the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built to your name,

9030.label: 1 Kings 8:45
9030.text: you must also hear from the heavens their prayer and their request for favor, and you must execute judgment for them.

9031.label: 1 Kings 8:46
9031.text: “In case they sin against you (for there is no man that does not sin), and you have to be incensed at them and abandon them to the enemy, and their captors actually carry them off captive to the land of the enemy distant or nearby;

9032.label: 1 Kings 8:47
9032.text: and they indeed come to their senses in the land where they have been carried off captive, and they actually return and make request to you for favor in the land of their captors, saying, ‘We have sinned and erred, we have acted wickedly’;

9033.label: 1 Kings 8:48
9033.text: and they indeed return to you with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies who carried them off captive, and they indeed pray to you in the direction of their land that you gave to their forefathers, the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built to your name;

9034.label: 1 Kings 8:49
9034.text: you must also hear from the heavens, your established place of dwelling, their prayer and their request for favor, and you must execute judgment for them,

9035.label: 1 Kings 8:50
9035.text: and you must forgive your people who had sinned against you and all their transgressions with which they transgressed against you; and you must make them objects of pity before their captors and they must pity them

9036.label: 1 Kings 8:51
9036.text: (for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out from Egypt, from inside the iron furnace),

9037.label: 1 Kings 8:52
9037.text: that your eyes may prove to be opened to the request for favor of your servant and to the request for favor of your people Israel, by listening to them in all for which they call to you.

9038.label: 1 Kings 8:53
9038.text: For you yourself separated them as your inheritance out of all the peoples of the earth, just as you have spoken by means of Moses your servant when you were bringing our forefathers out from Egypt, O Sovereign Lord Jehovah.”

9039.label: 1 Kings 8:54
9039.text: And it came about that, as soon as Solʹo·mon finished praying to Jehovah with all this prayer and request for favor, he rose up from before the altar of Jehovah, from bending down upon his knees with his palms spread out to the heavens;

9040.label: 1 Kings 8:55
9040.text: and he began to stand and bless all the congregation of Israel with a loud voice, saying:

9041.label: 1 Kings 8:56
9041.text: “Blessed be Jehovah, who has given a resting-place to his people Israel according to all that he has promised. There has not failed one word of all his good promise that he has promised by means of Moses his servant.

9042.label: 1 Kings 8:57
9042.text: May Jehovah our God prove to be with us just as he proved to be with our forefathers. May he neither leave us nor forsake us,

9043.label: 1 Kings 8:58
9043.text: so as to incline our heart to himself to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments and his regulations and his judicial decisions, which he gave in command to our forefathers.

9044.label: 1 Kings 8:59
9044.text: And may these words of mine with which I have made request for favor before Jehovah prove to be near to Jehovah our God by day and night, that he may execute judgment for his servant and judgment for his people Israel as it may require day by day;

9045.label: 1 Kings 8:60
9045.text: to the end that all the peoples of the earth may know that Jehovah is the [true] God. There is no other.

9046.label: 1 Kings 8:61
9046.text: And YOUR heart must prove to be complete with Jehovah our God by walking in his regulations and by keeping his commandments as at this day.”

9047.label: 1 Kings 8:62
9047.text: And the king and all Israel with him were offering a grand sacrifice before Jehovah.

9048.label: 1 Kings 8:63
9048.text: And Solʹo·mon proceeded to offer the communion sacrifices that he had to offer to Jehovah, twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep, that the king and all the sons of Israel might inaugurate the house of Jehovah.

9049.label: 1 Kings 8:64
9049.text: On that day the king had to sanctify the middle of the courtyard that is before the house of Jehovah, because there he had to render up the burnt sacrifice and the grain offering and the fat pieces of the communion sacrifices; for the copper altar that is before Jehovah was too small to contain the burnt sacrifice and the grain offering and the fat pieces of the communion sacrifices.

9050.label: 1 Kings 8:65
9050.text: And Solʹo·mon proceeded to carry on at that time the festival, and all Israel with him, a great congregation from the entering in of Haʹmath down to the torrent valley of Egypt, before Jehovah our God seven days and another seven days, fourteen days.

9051.label: 1 Kings 8:66
9051.text: On the eighth day he sent the people away; and they began to bless the king and to go to their homes, rejoicing and feeling merry of heart over all the goodness that Jehovah had performed for David his servant and for Israel his people.

9052.label: 1 Kings 9:1
9052.text: And it came about that, as soon as Solʹo·mon had finished building the house of Jehovah and the house of the king and every desirable thing of Solʹo·mon that he took delight in making,

9053.label: 1 Kings 9:2
9053.text: then Jehovah appeared to Solʹo·mon the second time, the same as he had appeared to him in Gibʹe·on.

9054.label: 1 Kings 9:3
9054.text: And Jehovah went on to say to him: “I have heard your prayer and your request for favor with which you requested favor before me. I have sanctified this house that you have built by putting my name there to time indefinite; and my eyes and my heart will certainly prove to be there always.

9055.label: 1 Kings 9:4
9055.text: And you, if you will walk before me, just as David your father walked, with integrity of heart and with uprightness by doing according to all that I have commanded you, and you will keep my regulations and my judicial decisions,

9056.label: 1 Kings 9:5
9056.text: I also shall indeed establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel to time indefinite, just as I promised David your father, saying, ‘Not a man of yours will be cut off from [sitting] upon the throne of Israel.’

9057.label: 1 Kings 9:6
9057.text: If YOU yourselves and YOUR sons should definitely turn back from following me and not keep my commandments and my statutes that I have put before YOU men, and YOU actually go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

9058.label: 1 Kings 9:7
9058.text: I will also cut Israel off from upon the surface of the ground that I have given to them; and the house that I have sanctified to my name I shall throw away from before me, and Israel will indeed become a proverbial saying and a taunt among all the peoples.

9059.label: 1 Kings 9:8
9059.text: And this house itself will become heaps of ruins. Everyone passing by it will stare in amazement and will certainly whistle and say, ‘For what reason did Jehovah do like that to this land and this house?’

9060.label: 1 Kings 9:9
9060.text: And they will have to say, ‘For the reason that they left Jehovah their God who had brought their forefathers out from the land of Egypt, and they proceeded to take hold of other gods and bow down to them and serve them. That is why Jehovah brought upon them all this calamity.’”

9061.label: 1 Kings 9:10
9061.text: And it came about at the end of twenty years, in which Solʹo·mon built the two houses, the house of Jehovah and the house of the king,

9062.label: 1 Kings 9:11
9062.text: (Hiʹram the king of Tyre had himself assisted Solʹo·mon with timbers of cedar trees and timbers of juniper trees and with gold as much as he delighted in,) that at that time King Solʹo·mon proceeded to give to Hiʹram twenty cities in the land of Galʹi·lee.

9063.label: 1 Kings 9:12
9063.text: Accordingly Hiʹram went out from Tyre to see the cities that Solʹo·mon had given him, and they were not just right in his eyes.

9064.label: 1 Kings 9:13
9064.text: So he said: “What sort of cities are these that you have given me, my brother?” And they came to be called the Land of Caʹbul down to this day.

9065.label: 1 Kings 9:14
9065.text: In the meantime Hiʹram sent to the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.

9066.label: 1 Kings 9:15
9066.text: Now this is the account of those conscripted for forced labor that King Solʹo·mon levied to build the house of Jehovah and his own house and the Mound and the wall of Jerusalem and Haʹzor and Me·gidʹdo and Geʹzer.

9067.label: 1 Kings 9:16
9067.text: (Pharʹaoh the king of Egypt himself had come up and then captured Geʹzer and burned it with fire, and the Caʹnaan·ites dwelling in the city he had killed. So he gave it as a parting gift to his daughter, the wife of Solʹo·mon.)

9068.label: 1 Kings 9:17
9068.text: And Solʹo·mon went on to build Geʹzer and Lower Beth-hoʹron,

9069.label: 1 Kings 9:18
9069.text: and Baʹal·ath and Taʹmar in the wilderness, in the land,

9070.label: 1 Kings 9:19
9070.text: and all the storage cities that became Solʹo·mon’s and the chariot cities and the cities for the horsemen, and the desirable things of Solʹo·mon that he had desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebʹa·non and in all the land of his dominion.

9071.label: 1 Kings 9:20
9071.text: As for all the people remaining over from the Amʹor·ites, the Hitʹtites, the Perʹiz·zites, the Hiʹvites and the Jebʹu·sites, who were no part of the sons of Israel,

9072.label: 1 Kings 9:21
9072.text: their sons who had been left over after them in the land whom the sons of Israel had been unable to devote to destruction, Solʹo·mon kept levying them for slavish forced labor until this day.

9073.label: 1 Kings 9:22
9073.text: And there were none of the sons of Israel that Solʹo·mon constituted slaves; for they were the warriors and his servants and his princes and his adjutants and chiefs of his charioteers and of his horsemen.

9074.label: 1 Kings 9:23
9074.text: These were the chiefs of the deputies who were over the work of Solʹo·mon, five hundred and fifty, the foremen over the people who were active in the work.

9075.label: 1 Kings 9:24
9075.text: However, Pharʹaoh’s daughter herself came up out of the City of David to her own house that he had built for her. It was then that he built the Mound.

9076.label: 1 Kings 9:25
9076.text: And Solʹo·mon continued three times in the year to offer up burnt sacrifices and communion sacrifices upon the altar that he had built for Jehovah, and there was a making of sacrificial smoke on the [altar], which was before Jehovah; and he completed the house.

9077.label: 1 Kings 9:26
9077.text: And there was a fleet of ships that King Solʹo·mon made in Eʹzi·on-geʹber, which is by Eʹloth, upon the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Eʹdom.

9078.label: 1 Kings 9:27
9078.text: And Hiʹram kept sending in the fleet of ships his own servants, seamen, having a knowledge of the sea, along with the servants of Solʹo·mon.

9079.label: 1 Kings 9:28
9079.text: And they proceeded to go to Oʹphir and take from there four hundred and twenty talents of gold and bring it in to King Solʹo·mon.

9080.label: 1 Kings 10:1
9080.text: Now the queen of Sheʹba was hearing the report about Solʹo·mon in connection with the name of Jehovah. So she came to test him with perplexing questions.

9081.label: 1 Kings 10:2
9081.text: Finally she arrived at Jerusalem with a very impressive train, camels carrying balsam oil and very much gold and precious stones; and she came on in to Solʹo·mon and began to speak to him all that happened to be close to her heart.

9082.label: 1 Kings 10:3
9082.text: Solʹo·mon, in turn, went on to tell her all her matters. There proved to be no matter hidden from the king that he did not tell her.

9083.label: 1 Kings 10:4
9083.text: When the queen of Sheʹba got to see all the wisdom of Solʹo·mon and the house that he had built,

9084.label: 1 Kings 10:5
9084.text: and the food of his table and the sitting of his servants and the table service of his waiters and their attire and his drinks and his burnt sacrifices that he regularly offered up at the house of Jehovah, then there proved to be no more spirit in her.

9085.label: 1 Kings 10:6
9085.text: So she said to the king: “True has the word proved to be that I heard in my own land about your matters and about your wisdom.

9086.label: 1 Kings 10:7
9086.text: And I did not put faith in the words until I had come that my own eyes might see; and, look! I had not been told the half. You have surpassed in wisdom and prosperity the things heard to which I listened.

9087.label: 1 Kings 10:8
9087.text: Happy are your men; happy are these servants of yours who are standing before you constantly, listening to your wisdom!

9088.label: 1 Kings 10:9
9088.text: May Jehovah your God come to be blessed, who has taken delight in you by putting you upon the throne of Israel; because Jehovah loves Israel to time indefinite, so that he appointed you as king to render judicial decision and righteousness.”

9089.label: 1 Kings 10:10
9089.text: Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold and a very great deal of balsam oil and precious stones. There never came anymore the like of that balsam oil for quantity such as the queen of Sheʹba gave to King Solʹo·mon.

9090.label: 1 Kings 10:11
9090.text: And Hiʹram’s fleet of ships that carried gold from Oʹphir also brought from Oʹphir timbers of algum trees in very great amount and precious stones.

9091.label: 1 Kings 10:12
9091.text: And the king proceeded to make out of the timbers of the algum trees supports for the house of Jehovah and for the house of the king, and also harps and stringed instruments for the singers. Timbers of algum trees like this have not come in nor have they been seen down to this day.

9092.label: 1 Kings 10:13
9092.text: And King Solʹo·mon himself gave the queen of Sheʹba all her delight for which she asked, apart from what he gave her according to the openhandedness of King Solʹo·mon. After that she turned about and went to her own land, she together with her servants.

9093.label: 1 Kings 10:14
9093.text: And the weight of the gold that came to Solʹo·mon in one year amounted up to six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,

9094.label: 1 Kings 10:15
9094.text: apart from the men of travel and the profit from the traders and all the kings of the Arabs and the governors of the land.

9095.label: 1 Kings 10:16
9095.text: And King Solʹo·mon went on to make two hundred large shields of alloyed gold (six hundred [shekels] of gold he proceeded to lay upon each large shield),

9096.label: 1 Kings 10:17
9096.text: and three hundred bucklers of alloyed gold (three miʹnas of gold he proceeded to lay upon each buckler ). Then the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebʹa·non.

9097.label: 1 Kings 10:18
9097.text: Further, the king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with refined gold.

9098.label: 1 Kings 10:19
9098.text: There were six steps to the throne, and the throne had a round canopy behind it, and there were armrests on this side and on that side by the place of sitting, and two lions were standing beside the armrests.

9099.label: 1 Kings 10:20
