9099.text: And there were twelve lions standing there upon the six steps, on this side and on that side. No other kingdom had any made just like it.

9100.label: 1 Kings 10:21
9100.text: And all the drinking vessels of King Solʹo·mon were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebʹa·non were of pure gold. There was nothing of silver; it was considered in the days of Solʹo·mon as nothing at all.

9101.label: 1 Kings 10:22
9101.text: For the king had a fleet of ships of Tarʹshish on the sea along with Hiʹram’s fleet of ships. Once every three years the fleet of ships of Tarʹshish would come carrying gold and silver, ivory, and apes and peacocks.

9102.label: 1 Kings 10:23
9102.text: So King Solʹo·mon was greater in riches and wisdom than all the other kings of the earth.

9103.label: 1 Kings 10:24
9103.text: And all the people of the earth were seeking the face of Solʹo·mon to hear his wisdom that God had put in his heart.

9104.label: 1 Kings 10:25
9104.text: And they were bringing each his gift, articles of silver and articles of gold and garments and armor and balsam oil, horses and mules, as a yearly matter of course.

9105.label: 1 Kings 10:26
9105.text: And Solʹo·mon kept gathering more chariots and steeds; and he came to have a thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand steeds, and he kept them stationed in the chariot cities and close by the king in Jerusalem.

9106.label: 1 Kings 10:27
9106.text: And the king came to make the silver in Jerusalem like the stones, and cedarwood he made like the sycamore trees that are in the She·pheʹlah for great quantity.

9107.label: 1 Kings 10:28
9107.text: And there was the export of the horses that Solʹo·mon had from Egypt, and the company of the king’s merchants would themselves take the horse drove for a price.

9108.label: 1 Kings 10:29
9108.text: And a chariot customarily came up and was exported from Egypt for six hundred silver pieces, and a horse for a hundred and fifty; and that was the way it was for all the kings of the Hitʹtites and the kings of Syria. It was by means of them that they did the exporting.

9109.label: 1 Kings 11:1
9109.text: And King Solʹo·mon himself loved many foreign wives along with the daughter of Pharʹaoh, Moʹab·ite, Amʹmon·ite, Eʹdom·ite, Si·doʹni·an [and] Hitʹtite women,

9110.label: 1 Kings 11:2
9110.text: from the nations of whom Jehovah had said to the sons of Israel: “YOU must not go in among them, and they themselves should not come in among YOU; truly they will incline YOUR heart to follow their gods.” It was to them that Solʹo·mon clung to love [them].

9111.label: 1 Kings 11:3
9111.text: And he came to have seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives gradually inclined his heart.

9112.label: 1 Kings 11:4
9112.text: And it came about in the time of Solʹo·mon’s growing old that his wives themselves had inclined his heart to follow other gods; and his heart did not prove to be complete with Jehovah his God like the heart of David his father.

9113.label: 1 Kings 11:5
9113.text: And Solʹo·mon began going after Ashʹto·reth the goddess of the Si·doʹni·ans and after Milʹcom the disgusting thing of the Amʹmon·ites.

9114.label: 1 Kings 11:6
9114.text: And Solʹo·mon began to do what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah, and he did not follow Jehovah fully like David his father.

9115.label: 1 Kings 11:7
9115.text: It was then that Solʹo·mon proceeded to build a high place to Cheʹmosh the disgusting thing of Moʹab on the mountain that was in front of Jerusalem, and to Moʹlech the disgusting thing of the sons of Amʹmon.

9116.label: 1 Kings 11:8
9116.text: And that was the way he did for all his foreign wives who were making sacrificial smoke and sacrificing to their gods.

9117.label: 1 Kings 11:9
9117.text: And Jehovah came to be incensed at Solʹo·mon, because his heart had inclined away from Jehovah the God of Israel, the one appearing to him twice.

9118.label: 1 Kings 11:10
9118.text: And respecting this thing he commanded him not to go after other gods; but he had not kept that which Jehovah had commanded.

9119.label: 1 Kings 11:11
9119.text: Jehovah now said to Solʹo·mon: “For the reason that this has taken place with you and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes that I laid in command upon you, I shall without fail rip the kingdom away from off you, and I shall certainly give it to your servant.

9120.label: 1 Kings 11:12
9120.text: However, in your days I shall not do it, for the sake of David your father. Out of the hand of your son I shall rip it away.

9121.label: 1 Kings 11:13
9121.text: Only it will not be all the kingdom that I shall rip away. One tribe I shall give to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem which I have chosen.”

9122.label: 1 Kings 11:14
9122.text: And Jehovah began to raise up a resister to Solʹo·mon, namely, Haʹdad the Eʹdom·ite of the offspring of the king. He was in Eʹdom.

9123.label: 1 Kings 11:15
9123.text: And it came about when David struck down Eʹdom, when Joʹab the chief of the army came up to bury those slain, that he tried to strike down every male in Eʹdom.

9124.label: 1 Kings 11:16
9124.text: (For it was six months that Joʹab and all Israel dwelt there until he had cut off every male in Eʹdom.)

9125.label: 1 Kings 11:17
9125.text: And Haʹdad went running away, he and some Eʹdom·ite men of the servants of his father with him, to come into Egypt, while Haʹdad was a young boy.

9126.label: 1 Kings 11:18
9126.text: So they rose up out of Midʹi·an and came into Paʹran and took men with them from Paʹran and came into Egypt to Pharʹaoh the king of Egypt, who then gave him a house. Also, bread he assigned to him, and land he gave him.

9127.label: 1 Kings 11:19
9127.text: And Haʹdad continued to find favor in the eyes of Pharʹaoh, so much that he gave him a wife, the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahʹpe·nes the lady.

9128.label: 1 Kings 11:20
9128.text: In time the sister of Tahʹpe·nes bore him Ge·nuʹbath his son, and Tahʹpe·nes got to wean him right inside the house of Pharʹaoh; and Ge·nuʹbath continued at the house of Pharʹaoh right among the sons of Pharʹaoh.

9129.label: 1 Kings 11:21
9129.text: And Haʹdad himself heard in Egypt that David had lain down with his forefathers and that Joʹab the chief of the army had died. So Haʹdad said to Pharʹaoh: “Send me away, that I may go to my own land.”

9130.label: 1 Kings 11:22
9130.text: But Pharʹaoh said to him: “What are you in need of while with me that here you are seeking to go to your own land?” To this he said: “Nothing; but you ought to send me away without fail.”

9131.label: 1 Kings 11:23
9131.text: And God proceeded to raise up to him another resister, namely, Reʹzon the son of E·liʹa·da, who had run away from Had·ad·eʹzer the king of Zoʹbah his lord.

9132.label: 1 Kings 11:24
9132.text: And he kept collecting men to his side and came to be chief of a marauder band, when David killed them. So they went to Damascus and took up dwelling in it and began reigning in Damascus.

9133.label: 1 Kings 11:25
9133.text: And he came to be a resister of Israel all the days of Solʹo·mon, and that along with the injury that Haʹdad did; and he had an abhorrence of Israel while he continued reigning over Syria.

9134.label: 1 Kings 11:26
9134.text: And there was Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat an Eʹphra·im·ite from Zerʹe·dah, a servant of Solʹo·mon, and his mother’s name was Ze·ruʹah, a widowed woman. He too began to lift up his hand against the king.

9135.label: 1 Kings 11:27
9135.text: And this is the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king: Solʹo·mon himself had built the Mound. He had closed up the gap of the City of David his father.

9136.label: 1 Kings 11:28
9136.text: Now the man Jer·o·boʹam was a valiant, mighty man. When Solʹo·mon got to see that the young man was a hard worker, he proceeded to make him overseer over all the compulsory service of the house of Joseph.

9137.label: 1 Kings 11:29
9137.text: And it came about at that particular time that Jer·o·boʹam himself went out from Jerusalem, and A·hiʹjah the Shiʹlo·nite the prophet got to find him on the road, and [A·hiʹjah] was covering himself with a new garment; and the two of them were by themselves in the field.

9138.label: 1 Kings 11:30
9138.text: A·hiʹjah now took hold of the new garment that was on him and ripped it into twelve pieces.

9139.label: 1 Kings 11:31
9139.text: And he went on to say to Jer·o·boʹam: “Take for yourself ten pieces; for this is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘Here I am ripping the kingdom out of the hand of Solʹo·mon, and I shall certainly give you ten tribes.

9140.label: 1 Kings 11:32
9140.text: And the one tribe is what will continue his for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.

9141.label: 1 Kings 11:33
9141.text: The reason why is that they have left me and begun to bow down to Ashʹto·reth the goddess of the Si·doʹni·ans, to Cheʹmosh the god of Moʹab and to Milʹcom the god of the sons of Amʹmon; and they have not walked in my ways by doing what is right in my eyes and my statutes and my judicial decisions like David his father.

9142.label: 1 Kings 11:34
9142.text: But I shall not take the entire kingdom out of his hand, because a chieftain I shall set him for all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant whom I chose, because he kept my commandments and my statutes.

9143.label: 1 Kings 11:35
9143.text: And I shall certainly take the kingship out of the hand of his son and give it to you, even ten tribes.

9144.label: 1 Kings 11:36
9144.text: And to his son I shall give one tribe, in order that David my servant may continue having a lamp always before me in Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen for myself to put my name there.

9145.label: 1 Kings 11:37
9145.text: And you are the one that I shall take, and you will indeed reign over all that your soul craves, and you will certainly become king over Israel.

9146.label: 1 Kings 11:38
9146.text: And it must occur that, if you obey all that I shall command you, and you do walk in my ways and actually do what is right in my eyes by keeping my statutes and my commandments, just as David my servant did, I will also prove to be with you, and I will build you a lasting house, just as I have built for David, and I will give you Israel.

9147.label: 1 Kings 11:39
9147.text: And I shall humiliate the offspring of David on account of this, only not always.’”

9148.label: 1 Kings 11:40
9148.text: And Solʹo·mon began seeking to put Jer·o·boʹam to death. So Jer·o·boʹam got up and went running off to Egypt to Shiʹshak the king of Egypt, and he continued in Egypt until Solʹo·mon’s death.

9149.label: 1 Kings 11:41
9149.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Solʹo·mon and all that he did and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the affairs of Solʹo·mon?

9150.label: 1 Kings 11:42
9150.text: And the days that Solʹo·mon had reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years.

9151.label: 1 Kings 11:43
9151.text: Then Solʹo·mon lay down with his forefathers, and was buried in the City of David his father; and Re·ho·boʹam his son began to reign in place of him.

9152.label: 1 Kings 12:1
9152.text: And Re·ho·boʹam proceeded to go to Sheʹchem, for it was to Sheʹchem that all Israel came to make him king.

9153.label: 1 Kings 12:2
9153.text: And it came about that as soon as Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat heard of it while he was yet in Egypt (because he had run off on account of King Solʹo·mon, that Jer·o·boʹam might dwell in Egypt),

9154.label: 1 Kings 12:3
9154.text: then they sent and called him. After that Jer·o·boʹam and all the congregation of Israel came and began to speak to Re·ho·boʹam, saying:

9155.label: 1 Kings 12:4
9155.text: “Your father, for his part, made our yoke hard, and, as for you, now make the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke that he put upon us lighter, and we shall serve you.”

9156.label: 1 Kings 12:5
9156.text: At this he said to them: “Go away for three days and return to me.” So the people went away.

9157.label: 1 Kings 12:6
9157.text: And King Re·ho·boʹam began to take counsel with the older men who had continued attending upon Solʹo·mon his father while he continued alive, saying: “How are YOU advising to reply to this people?”

9158.label: 1 Kings 12:7
9158.text: Accordingly they spoke to him, saying: “If today you would prove yourself a servant to this people and actually serve them, you must also answer them and speak to them with good words; and they will be bound to become your servants always.”

9159.label: 1 Kings 12:8
9159.text: However, he left the counsel of the older men with which they had advised him, and he began to take counsel with the young men that had grown up with him, who were the ones attending upon him.

9160.label: 1 Kings 12:9
9160.text: And he went on to say to them: “What is it that YOU are offering in counsel that we may reply to this people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Make the yoke that your father put upon us lighter’?”

9161.label: 1 Kings 12:10
9161.text: In turn the young men that had grown up with him spoke to him, saying: “This is what you should say to this people who have spoken to you, saying, ‘Your father, for his part, made our yoke heavy, but, as for you, make it lighter upon us’; this is what you should speak to them, ‘My little finger itself will certainly be thicker than my father’s hips.

9162.label: 1 Kings 12:11
9162.text: And now my father, for his part, loaded upon YOU a heavy yoke; but I, for my part, shall add to YOUR yoke. My father, for his part, chastised YOU with whips, but I, for my part, shall chastise YOU with scourges.’”

9163.label: 1 Kings 12:12
9163.text: And Jer·o·boʹam and all the people proceeded to come to Re·ho·boʹam on the third day, just as the king had spoken, saying: “Return to me on the third day.”

9164.label: 1 Kings 12:13
9164.text: And the king began to answer the people harshly, and to leave the counsel of the older men who had counseled him.

9165.label: 1 Kings 12:14
9165.text: And he went on to speak to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying: “My father, for his part, made YOUR yoke heavy, but I, for my part, shall add to YOUR yoke. My father, for his part, chastised YOU with whips, but I, for my part, shall chastise YOU with scourges.”

9166.label: 1 Kings 12:15
9166.text: And the king did not listen to the people, because the turn of affairs took place at the instance of Jehovah, in order that he might indeed carry out his word that Jehovah had spoken by means of A·hiʹjah the Shiʹlo·nite to Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat.

9167.label: 1 Kings 12:16
9167.text: When all Israel got to see that the king had not listened to them, then the people replied to the king, saying: “What share do we have in David? And there is no inheritance in the son of Jesʹse. To your gods, O Israel. Now see to your own house, O David!” With that Israel began to go to their tents.

9168.label: 1 Kings 12:17
9168.text: As for the sons of Israel that were dwelling in the cities of Judah, Re·ho·boʹam continued to reign over them.

9169.label: 1 Kings 12:18
9169.text: Subsequently King Re·ho·boʹam sent A·doʹram, who was over those conscripted for forced labor, but all Israel pelted him with stones, so that he died. And King Re·ho·boʹam himself managed to get up into the chariot to flee to Jerusalem.

9170.label: 1 Kings 12:19
9170.text: And the Israelites kept up their revolt against the house of David down to this day.

9171.label: 1 Kings 12:20
9171.text: And it came about that as soon as all Israel heard that Jer·o·boʹam had returned, they at once sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. None became a follower of the house of David except the tribe of Judah by itself.

9172.label: 1 Kings 12:21
9172.text: When Re·ho·boʹam arrived at Jerusalem, he immediately congregated all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand choice men able-bodied for war, to fight against the house of Israel, so as to bring the kingship back to Re·ho·boʹam the son of Solʹo·mon.

9173.label: 1 Kings 12:22
9173.text: Then the word of the [true] God came to She·maiʹah the man of the [true] God, saying:

9174.label: 1 Kings 12:23
9174.text: “Say to Re·ho·boʹam the son of Solʹo·mon the king of Judah and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and the rest of the people,

9175.label: 1 Kings 12:24
9175.text: ‘This is what Jehovah has said: “YOU must not go up and fight against YOUR brothers the sons of Israel. Go back each one to his house, for it is at the instance of myself that this thing has been brought about.”’” So they obeyed the word of Jehovah, and went back home according to the word of Jehovah.

9176.label: 1 Kings 12:25
9176.text: And Jer·o·boʹam proceeded to build Sheʹchem in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im and to dwell in it. Then he went forth from there and built Pe·nuʹel.

9177.label: 1 Kings 12:26
9177.text: And Jer·o·boʹam began to say in his heart: “Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.

9178.label: 1 Kings 12:27
9178.text: If this people continues going up to render sacrifices in the house of Jehovah in Jerusalem, the heart of this people will also be bound to return to their lord, Re·ho·boʹam the king of Judah; and they will certainly kill me and return to Re·ho·boʹam the king of Judah.”

9179.label: 1 Kings 12:28
9179.text: Consequently the king took counsel and made two golden calves and said to the people: “It is too much for YOU to go up to Jerusalem. Here is your God, O Israel, that brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”

9180.label: 1 Kings 12:29
9180.text: Then he placed the one in Bethʹel, and the other he put in Dan.

9181.label: 1 Kings 12:30
9181.text: And this thing came to be a cause for sin, and the people began to go before the one as far as Dan.

9182.label: 1 Kings 12:31
9182.text: And he began to make a house of high places and to make priests from the people in general, who did not happen to be of the sons of Leʹvi.

9183.label: 1 Kings 12:32
9183.text: And Jer·o·boʹam went on to make a festival in the eighth month on the fifteenth day of the month, like the festival that was in Judah, that he might make offerings upon the altar that he had made in Bethʹel, to sacrifice to the calves that he had made; and he put in attendance at Bethʹel the priests of the high places that he had made.

9184.label: 1 Kings 12:33
9184.text: And he began to make offerings upon the altar that he had made in Bethʹel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the month that he had invented by himself; and he proceeded to make a festival for the sons of Israel and to make offerings upon the altar to make sacrificial smoke.

9185.label: 1 Kings 13:1
9185.text: And here there was a man of God that had come out of Judah by the word of Jehovah to Bethʹel, while Jer·o·boʹam was standing by the altar to make sacrificial smoke.

9186.label: 1 Kings 13:2
9186.text: Then he called out against the altar by the word of Jehovah and said: “O altar, altar, this is what Jehovah has said, ‘Look! A son born to the house of David, whose name is Jo·siʹah! And he will certainly sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places that are making sacrificial smoke upon you, and men’s bones he will burn upon you.’”

9187.label: 1 Kings 13:3
9187.text: And he gave a portent on that day, saying: “This is the portent of which Jehovah has spoken: Look! The altar is ripped apart, and the fatty ashes that are upon it will certainly be spilled out.”

9188.label: 1 Kings 13:4
9188.text: And it came about that, as soon as the king heard the word of the man of the [true] God that he had called out against the altar in Bethʹel, Jer·o·boʹam at once thrust out his hand from off the altar, saying: “YOU men, grab hold of him!” Immediately his hand that he had thrust out against him became dried up, and he was not able to draw it back to himself.

9189.label: 1 Kings 13:5
9189.text: And the altar itself was ripped apart so that the fatty ashes were spilled out from the altar, according to the portent that the man of the [true] God had given by the word of Jehovah.

9190.label: 1 Kings 13:6
9190.text: The king now answered and said to the man of the [true] God: “Soften, please, the face of Jehovah your God and pray in my behalf that my hand may be restored to me.” At this the man of the [true] God softened the face of Jehovah, so that the king’s hand was restored to him, and it came to be as at first.

9191.label: 1 Kings 13:7
9191.text: And the king went on to say to the man of the [true] God: “Do come with me to the house and take sustenance, and let me give you a gift.”

9192.label: 1 Kings 13:8
9192.text: But the man of the [true] God said to the king: “If you gave me half of your house I would not come with you and eat bread or drink water in this place.

9193.label: 1 Kings 13:9
9193.text: For that is the way he commanded me by the word of Jehovah, saying, ‘You must not eat bread or drink water, and you must not return by the way that you went.’”

9194.label: 1 Kings 13:10
9194.text: And he began to go by another way, and he did not return by the way by which he had come to Bethʹel.

9195.label: 1 Kings 13:11
9195.text: And a certain old prophet was dwelling in Bethʹel, and his sons now came in and related to him all the work that the man of the [true] God had done that day in Bethʹel [and] the words that he had spoken to the king, and they went on relating them to their father.

9196.label: 1 Kings 13:12
9196.text: Then their father spoke to them: “Which way, then, did he go?” So his sons showed him the way that the man of the [true] God that had come out of Judah had gone.

9197.label: 1 Kings 13:13
9197.text: He now said to his sons: “Saddle the ass for me.” Accordingly they saddled the ass for him, and he went riding on it.

9198.label: 1 Kings 13:14
9198.text: And he went following the man of the [true] God and got to find him sitting under the big tree. Then he said to him: “Are you the man of the [true] God who has come out of Judah?” to which he said: “I am.”

9199.label: 1 Kings 13:15
9199.text: And he went on to say to him: “Go with me to the house and eat bread.”

9200.label: 1 Kings 13:16
9200.text: But he said: “I am not able to go back with you or to come in with you, and I may not eat bread or drink water with you in this place.

9201.label: 1 Kings 13:17
9201.text: For it has been spoken to me by the word of Jehovah, ‘You must not eat bread or drink water there. You must not go back again by the way by which you went.’”

9202.label: 1 Kings 13:18
9202.text: At this he said to him: “I too am a prophet like you, and an angel himself spoke to me by the word of Jehovah, saying, ‘Have him come back with you to your house that he may eat bread and drink water.’” (He deceived him.)

9203.label: 1 Kings 13:19
9203.text: So he went back with him that he might eat bread in his house and drink water.

9204.label: 1 Kings 13:20
9204.text: And it came about, while they were sitting at the table, that the word of Jehovah came to the prophet that had brought him back;

9205.label: 1 Kings 13:21
9205.text: and he began to call out to the man of the [true] God that had come out of Judah, saying: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘For the reason that you rebelled against the order of Jehovah and did not keep the commandment with which Jehovah your God commanded you,

9206.label: 1 Kings 13:22
9206.text: but you went back that you might eat bread and drink water in the place about which he spoke to you: “Do not eat bread or drink water,” your dead body will not come into the burial place of your forefathers.’”

9207.label: 1 Kings 13:23
9207.text: And it came about after his eating bread and after his drinking that he at once saddled for him the ass, that is, for the prophet whom he had brought back.

9208.label: 1 Kings 13:24
9208.text: And he got on his way. Later a lion found him on the road and put him to death, and his dead body came to be thrown onto the road. And the ass was standing beside it, and the lion was standing beside the dead body.

9209.label: 1 Kings 13:25
9209.text: And here there were men passing by, so that they got to see the dead body thrown onto the road and the lion standing beside the dead body. Then they came in and spoke of it in the city in which the old prophet was dwelling.

9210.label: 1 Kings 13:26
9210.text: When the prophet that had brought him back from the way heard of it, he immediately said: “It is the man of the [true] God that rebelled against the order of Jehovah; and so Jehovah gave him to the lion, that he might crush him and put him to death, according to the word of Jehovah that he spoke to him.”

9211.label: 1 Kings 13:27
9211.text: And he went on to speak to his sons, saying: “Saddle the ass for me.” So they saddled it.

9212.label: 1 Kings 13:28
9212.text: Then he got on his way and found the dead body of him thrown onto the road with the ass and the lion standing beside the dead body. The lion had not eaten the dead body, nor had it crushed the ass.

9213.label: 1 Kings 13:29
9213.text: And the prophet proceeded to lift up the dead body of the man of the [true] God and to deposit him upon the ass and to bring him back. Thus he came into the city of the old prophet to bewail and bury him.

9214.label: 1 Kings 13:30
9214.text: Accordingly he deposited his dead body in his own burial place; and they kept wailing over him: “Too bad, my brother!”

9215.label: 1 Kings 13:31
9215.text: And it came about after his burying him that he went on to say to his sons: “When I die YOU must bury me in the burial place in which the man of the [true] God is buried. Beside his bones deposit my own bones.

9216.label: 1 Kings 13:32
9216.text: For without fail the word that he called out by the word of Jehovah against the altar that is in Bethʹel and against all the houses of the high places that are in the cities of Sa·marʹi·a will take place.”

9217.label: 1 Kings 13:33
9217.text: After this thing Jer·o·boʹam did not turn back from his bad way, but he again went making priests of high places from the people in general. As for anyone delighting in it, he would fill his hand with power, [saying]: “And let him become [one of the] priests of high places.”

9218.label: 1 Kings 13:34
9218.text: And in this thing there came to be a cause of sin on the part of the household of Jer·o·boʹam and an occasion for effacing them and annihilating them off the surface of the ground.

9219.label: 1 Kings 14:1
9219.text: At that particular time A·biʹjah the son of Jer·o·boʹam fell sick.

9220.label: 1 Kings 14:2
9220.text: So Jer·o·boʹam said to his wife: “Rise up, please, and you must disguise yourself that they may not know that you are the wife of Jer·o·boʹam, and you must go to Shiʹloh. Look! There is where A·hiʹjah the prophet is. He is the one that spoke with reference to me as to becoming king over this people.

9221.label: 1 Kings 14:3
9221.text: And you must take in your hand ten loaves of bread and sprinkled cakes and a flask of honey, and you must come in to him. He it is that will certainly tell you what is going to happen to the boy.”

9222.label: 1 Kings 14:4
9222.text: And the wife of Jer·o·boʹam proceeded to do so. Consequently she rose up and went to Shiʹloh and came to the house of A·hiʹjah. Now A·hiʹjah himself was unable to see, for his eyes had set because of his age.

9223.label: 1 Kings 14:5
9223.text: And Jehovah himself had said to A·hiʹjah: “Here is the wife of Jer·o·boʹam coming to apply for a word from you regarding her son; for he is sick. This way and that is how you should speak to her. And it will occur that as soon as she arrives, she will be making herself unrecognizable.”

9224.label: 1 Kings 14:6
9224.text: And it came about that as soon as A·hiʹjah heard the sound of her feet as she was coming into the entrance, he began to say: “Come in, you wife of Jer·o·boʹam. Why is it that you are making yourself unrecognizable while I am being sent to you with a severe message?

9225.label: 1 Kings 14:7
9225.text: Go, say to Jer·o·boʹam, ‘This is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said: “For the reason that I raised you up out of the middle of your people, that I might constitute you a leader over my people Israel,

9226.label: 1 Kings 14:8
9226.text: and I went on to rip the kingdom away from the house of David and give it to you, and you have not become like my servant David, who kept my commandments and who walked after me with all his heart by doing only what was right in my eyes,

9227.label: 1 Kings 14:9
9227.text: but you began to act worse than all those who happened to be prior to you, and you went and made for yourself another god and molten images to offend me, and it is I whom you have cast behind your back;

9228.label: 1 Kings 14:10
9228.text: for that reason here I am bringing calamity upon the house of Jer·o·boʹam, and I shall certainly cut off from Jer·o·boʹam anyone urinating against a wall, a helpless and worthless one in Israel; and I shall indeed make a clean sweep behind the house of Jer·o·boʹam, just as one clears away the dung until it is disposed of.

9229.label: 1 Kings 14:11
9229.text: The one dying of Jer·o·boʹam’s in the city, the dogs will eat; and the one dying in the field, the fowls of the heavens will eat, because Jehovah himself has spoken it.”’

9230.label: 1 Kings 14:12
9230.text: “And you yourself, rise up, go to your house. When your feet come into the city the child will certainly die.

9231.label: 1 Kings 14:13
9231.text: And all Israel will indeed bewail him and bury him, because this one alone of Jer·o·boʹam’s will come into a burial place; for the reason that something good toward Jehovah the God of Israel has been found in him in the house of Jer·o·boʹam.

9232.label: 1 Kings 14:14
9232.text: And Jehovah will certainly raise up to himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jer·o·boʹam the said day, and what if right now?

9233.label: 1 Kings 14:15
9233.text: And Jehovah will indeed strike Israel down, just as the reed sways in the water; and he will certainly uproot Israel off this good ground that he gave to their forefathers, and he will indeed scatter them beyond the River, for the reason that they made their sacred poles, so offending Jehovah.

9234.label: 1 Kings 14:16
9234.text: And he will give Israel up on account of the sins of Jer·o·boʹam with which he sinned and with which he caused Israel to sin.”

9235.label: 1 Kings 14:17
9235.text: At that Jer·o·boʹam’s wife rose up and went her way and came to Tirʹzah. As she was arriving at the threshold of the house, the boy himself died.

9236.label: 1 Kings 14:18
9236.text: So they buried him, and all Israel went wailing for him, according to Jehovah’s word that he had spoken by means of his servant A·hiʹjah the prophet.

9237.label: 1 Kings 14:19
9237.text: And the rest of the affairs of Jer·o·boʹam, how he warred and how he reigned, there they are written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel.

9238.label: 1 Kings 14:20
9238.text: And the days that Jer·o·boʹam reigned were twenty-two years, after which he lay down with his forefathers; and Naʹdab his son began to reign in place of him.

9239.label: 1 Kings 14:21
9239.text: As for Re·ho·boʹam the son of Solʹo·mon, he had become king in Judah. Forty-one years old Re·ho·boʹam was when he began to reign, and seventeen years he reigned in Jerusalem, the city that Jehovah had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. And his mother’s name was Naʹa·mah the Amʹmon·it·ess.

9240.label: 1 Kings 14:22
9240.text: And Judah went on doing what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah, so that they incited him to jealousy more than all that their forefathers had done by their sins with which they sinned.

9241.label: 1 Kings 14:23
9241.text: And they too kept building for themselves high places and sacred pillars and sacred poles upon every high hill and under every luxuriant tree.

9242.label: 1 Kings 14:24
9242.text: And even the male temple prostitute proved to be in the land. They acted according to all the detestable things of the nations whom Jehovah had driven out from before the sons of Israel.

9243.label: 1 Kings 14:25
9243.text: And it came about in the fifth year of King Re·ho·boʹam that Shiʹshak the king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.

9244.label: 1 Kings 14:26
9244.text: And he got to take the treasures of the house of Jehovah and the treasures of the house of the king; and everything he took. And he went on to take all the gold shields that Solʹo·mon had made.

9245.label: 1 Kings 14:27
9245.text: Consequently King Re·ho·boʹam made in place of them copper shields, and he committed them to the control of the chiefs of the runners, the guards of the entrance of the king’s house.

9246.label: 1 Kings 14:28
9246.text: And it would occur that as often as the king came to the house of Jehovah, the runners would carry them, and they returned them to the guard chamber of the runners.

9247.label: 1 Kings 14:29
9247.text: And the rest of the affairs of Re·ho·boʹam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the times of the kings of Judah?

9248.label: 1 Kings 14:30
9248.text: And warfare itself took place between Re·ho·boʹam and Jer·o·boʹam always.

9249.label: 1 Kings 14:31
9249.text: Finally Re·ho·boʹam lay down with his forefathers and was buried with his forefathers in the City of David. And his mother’s name was Naʹa·mah the Amʹmon·it·ess. And A·biʹjam his son began to reign in place of him.

9250.label: 1 Kings 15:1
9250.text: And in the eighteenth year of King Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, A·biʹjam became king over Judah.

9251.label: 1 Kings 15:2
9251.text: Three years he reigned in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was Maʹa·cah the granddaughter of A·bishʹa·lom.

9252.label: 1 Kings 15:3
9252.text: And he went on walking in all the sins of his father that he did prior to him; and his heart did not prove to be complete with Jehovah his God, like the heart of David his forefather.

9253.label: 1 Kings 15:4
9253.text: For, on account of David, Jehovah his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem by raising his son up after him and keeping Jerusalem in existence,

9254.label: 1 Kings 15:5
9254.text: because David did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, and he did not turn aside from anything that He had commanded him all the days of his life, only in the matter of U·riʹah the Hitʹtite.

9255.label: 1 Kings 15:6
9255.text: And warfare itself took place between Re·ho·boʹam and Jer·o·boʹam all the days of his life.

9256.label: 1 Kings 15:7
9256.text: As for the rest of the affairs of A·biʹjam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah? There was warfare also that took place between A·biʹjam and Jer·o·boʹam.

9257.label: 1 Kings 15:8
9257.text: Finally A·biʹjam lay down with his forefathers and they buried him in the City of David; and Aʹsa his son began to reign in place of him.

9258.label: 1 Kings 15:9
9258.text: In the twentieth year of Jer·o·boʹam the king of Israel, Aʹsa reigned as king of Judah.

9259.label: 1 Kings 15:10
9259.text: And forty-one years he reigned in Jerusalem; and his grandmother’s name was Maʹa·cah the granddaughter of A·bishʹa·lom.

9260.label: 1 Kings 15:11
9260.text: And Aʹsa proceeded to do what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, like David his forefather.

9261.label: 1 Kings 15:12
9261.text: Accordingly he had the male temple prostitutes pass out of the land and removed all the dungy idols that his forefathers had made.

9262.label: 1 Kings 15:13
9262.text: As for even Maʹa·cah his grandmother, he went on to remove her from [being] lady, because she had made a horrible idol to the sacred pole; after which Aʹsa cut down her horrible idol and burned it at the torrent valley of Kidʹron.

9263.label: 1 Kings 15:14
9263.text: And the high places he did not remove. Nevertheless, Aʹsa’s heart itself proved to be complete with Jehovah all his days.

9264.label: 1 Kings 15:15
9264.text: And he began to bring in the things made holy by his father and the things made holy by himself into the house of Jehovah, silver and gold and articles.

9265.label: 1 Kings 15:16
9265.text: And warfare itself took place between Aʹsa and Baʹa·sha the king of Israel all their days.

9266.label: 1 Kings 15:17
9266.text: So Baʹa·sha the king of Israel came up against Judah and began to build Raʹmah, to allow no one to go out or come in to Aʹsa the king of Judah.

9267.label: 1 Kings 15:18
9267.text: At that Aʹsa took all the silver and the gold that were left in the treasures of the house of Jehovah and the treasures of the house of the king and put them in the hand of his servants; and King Aʹsa now sent them to Ben-haʹdad the son of Tab·rimʹmon the son of Heʹzi·on, the king of Syria, who was dwelling in Damascus, saying:

9268.label: 1 Kings 15:19
9268.text: “There is a covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Here I have sent you a present of silver and gold. Come, do break your covenant with Baʹa·sha the king of Israel, that he may withdraw from me.”

9269.label: 1 Kings 15:20
9269.text: Accordingly Ben-haʹdad listened to King Aʹsa and sent the chiefs of the military forces that were his against the cities of Israel and went striking down Iʹjon and Dan and Aʹbel-beth-maʹa·cah and all Chinʹne·reth, as far as all the land of Naphʹta·li.

9270.label: 1 Kings 15:21
9270.text: And it came about that as soon as Baʹa·sha heard of it, he immediately quit building Raʹmah and continued dwelling in Tirʹzah.

9271.label: 1 Kings 15:22
9271.text: And King Aʹsa, for his part, summoned all Judah —there was none exempt—and they proceeded to carry the stones of Raʹmah and the timbers of it, with which Baʹa·sha had been building; and King Aʹsa began to build with them Geʹba in Benjamin, and Mizʹpah.

9272.label: 1 Kings 15:23
9272.text: As for the rest of all the affairs of Aʹsa and all his mightiness and all that he did and the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah? Only at the time of his growing old he got diseased in his feet.

9273.label: 1 Kings 15:24
9273.text: Finally Aʹsa lay down with his forefathers and was buried with his forefathers in the City of David his forefather; and Je·hoshʹa·phat his son began to reign in place of him.

9274.label: 1 Kings 15:25
9274.text: As for Naʹdab the son of Jer·o·boʹam, he became king over Israel in the second year of Aʹsa the king of Judah; and he continued to reign over Israel two years.

9275.label: 1 Kings 15:26
9275.text: And he kept doing what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah and went on walking in the way of his father and in his sin with which he caused Israel to sin.

9276.label: 1 Kings 15:27
9276.text: And Baʹa·sha the son of A·hiʹjah of the house of Isʹsa·char began to conspire against him; and Baʹa·sha got to strike him down at Gibʹbe·thon, which belonged to the Phi·lisʹtines, while Naʹdab and all Israel were besieging Gibʹbe·thon.

9277.label: 1 Kings 15:28
9277.text: So Baʹa·sha put him to death in the third year of Aʹsa the king of Judah and began to reign in place of him.

9278.label: 1 Kings 15:29
9278.text: And it came about that as soon as he became king, he struck down all the house of Jer·o·boʹam. He did not let anyone breathing remain of Jer·o·boʹam’s until he had annihilated them, according to Jehovah’s word that he had spoken by means of his servant A·hiʹjah the Shiʹlo·nite,

9279.label: 1 Kings 15:30
9279.text: on account of the sins of Jer·o·boʹam with which he sinned and with which he caused Israel to sin [and] by his offensiveness with which he offended Jehovah the God of Israel.

9280.label: 1 Kings 15:31
9280.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Naʹdab and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9281.label: 1 Kings 15:32
9281.text: And warfare itself took place between Aʹsa and Baʹa·sha the king of Israel all their days.

9282.label: 1 Kings 15:33
9282.text: In the third year of Aʹsa the king of Judah, Baʹa·sha the son of A·hiʹjah became king over all Israel in Tirʹzah for twenty-four years.

9283.label: 1 Kings 15:34
9283.text: And he kept doing what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah and went walking in the way of Jer·o·boʹam and in his sin with which he caused Israel to sin.

9284.label: 1 Kings 16:1
9284.text: The word of Jehovah now came to Jeʹhu the son of Ha·naʹni against Baʹa·sha, saying:

9285.label: 1 Kings 16:2
9285.text: “Inasmuch as I raised you up out of the dust that I might constitute you leader over my people Israel, but you went walking in the way of Jer·o·boʹam and so caused my people Israel to sin by offending me with their sins,

9286.label: 1 Kings 16:3
9286.text: here I am making a clean sweep after Baʹa·sha and after his house, and I shall certainly constitute his house like the house of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat.

9287.label: 1 Kings 16:4
9287.text: Anyone of Baʹa·sha that is dying in the city the dogs will eat; and anyone of his that is dying in the field the fowls of the heavens will eat.”

9288.label: 1 Kings 16:5
9288.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Baʹa·sha and what he did and his mightiness, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9289.label: 1 Kings 16:6
9289.text: Finally Baʹa·sha lay down with his forefathers and was buried in Tirʹzah; and Eʹlah his son began to reign in place of him.

9290.label: 1 Kings 16:7
9290.text: And also by means of Jeʹhu the son of Ha·naʹni the prophet, Jehovah’s word itself had come against Baʹa·sha and his house, both because of all the badness that he committed in the eyes of Jehovah by offending him with the work of his hands, that it might become like the house of Jer·o·boʹam, and because he struck him down.

9291.label: 1 Kings 16:8
9291.text: In the twenty-sixth year of Aʹsa the king of Judah, Eʹlah the son of Baʹa·sha became king over Israel in Tirʹzah for two years.

9292.label: 1 Kings 16:9
9292.text: And his servant Zimʹri the chief of half the chariots began to conspire against him, while he was in Tirʹzah drinking himself drunk at the house of Arʹza, who was over the household in Tirʹzah.

9293.label: 1 Kings 16:10
9293.text: And Zimʹri proceeded to come in and strike him down and put him to death in the twenty-seventh year of Aʹsa the king of Judah, and he began to reign in place of him.

9294.label: 1 Kings 16:11
9294.text: And it came about that when he began to reign, as soon as he sat down upon his throne, he struck down all the house of Baʹa·sha. He did not let anyone of his remain that urinates against a wall or his avengers of blood or his friends.

9295.label: 1 Kings 16:12
9295.text: Thus Zimʹri annihilated the whole house of Baʹa·sha, according to the word of Jehovah that he had spoken against Baʹa·sha by means of Jeʹhu the prophet,

9296.label: 1 Kings 16:13
9296.text: on account of all the sins of Baʹa·sha and the sins of Eʹlah his son with which they sinned and with which they caused Israel to sin by offending Jehovah the God of Israel with their vain idols.

9297.label: 1 Kings 16:14
9297.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Eʹlah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9298.label: 1 Kings 16:15
9298.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Aʹsa the king of Judah, Zimʹri became king for seven days in Tirʹzah, while the people were encamping against Gibʹbe·thon, which belonged to the Phi·lisʹtines.

9299.label: 1 Kings 16:16
9299.text: In time the people that were encamped heard it said: “Zimʹri has conspired and also struck down the king.” So all Israel made Omʹri, the chief of the army, king over Israel on that day in the camp.

9300.label: 1 Kings 16:17
9300.text: Omʹri and all Israel with him now went on up from Gibʹbe·thon and began to lay siege to Tirʹzah.

9301.label: 1 Kings 16:18
9301.text: And it came about that as soon as Zimʹri saw that the city had been captured, he then came into the dwelling tower of the king’s house and burned the king’s house over himself with fire, so that he died,

9302.label: 1 Kings 16:19
9302.text: for the sins of his with which he had sinned by doing what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah by walking in the way of Jer·o·boʹam and in his sin which he did by causing Israel to sin.

9303.label: 1 Kings 16:20
9303.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Zimʹri and his conspiracy with which he conspired, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9304.label: 1 Kings 16:21
9304.text: It was then that the people of Israel began to divide themselves into two parts. There was one part of the people that became followers of Tibʹni the son of Giʹnath, to make him king, and the other part followers of Omʹri.

9305.label: 1 Kings 16:22
9305.text: Finally the people that were following Omʹri overcame the people that were following Tibʹni the son of Giʹnath; so that Tibʹni met death, and Omʹri began to reign.

9306.label: 1 Kings 16:23
9306.text: In the thirty-first year of Aʹsa the king of Judah, Omʹri became king over Israel for twelve years. In Tirʹzah he reigned six years.

9307.label: 1 Kings 16:24
9307.text: And he proceeded to buy the mountain of Sa·marʹi·a from Sheʹmer for two talents of silver, and began to build [on] the mountain and call the name of the city that he built by the name of Sheʹmer the master of the mountain, Sa·marʹi·a.

9308.label: 1 Kings 16:25
9308.text: And Omʹri kept doing what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah and came to do worse than all who were prior to him.

9309.label: 1 Kings 16:26
9309.text: And he went walking in all the way of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat and in his sin with which he caused Israel to sin by offending Jehovah the God of Israel with their vain idols.

9310.label: 1 Kings 16:27
9310.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Omʹri, what he did and his mightiness with which he acted, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9311.label: 1 Kings 16:28
9311.text: Finally Omʹri lay down with his forefathers and was buried in Sa·marʹi·a; and Aʹhab his son began to reign in place of him.

9312.label: 1 Kings 16:29
9312.text: And as for Aʹhab the son of Omʹri, he became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Aʹsa the king of Judah; and Aʹhab the son of Omʹri continued to reign over Israel in Sa·marʹi·a twenty-two years.

9313.label: 1 Kings 16:30
9313.text: And Aʹhab the son of Omʹri proceeded to do worse in the eyes of Jehovah than all those who were prior to him.

9314.label: 1 Kings 16:31
9314.text: And it came about that, [as if it were] the most trivial thing for him to walk in the sins of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, he now took as wife Jezʹe·bel the daughter of Eth·baʹal the king of the Si·doʹni·ans and began to go and serve Baʹal and to bow down to him.

9315.label: 1 Kings 16:32
9315.text: Further, he set up an altar to Baʹal at the house of Baʹal that he built in Sa·marʹi·a.

9316.label: 1 Kings 16:33
9316.text: And Aʹhab went on to make the sacred pole; and Aʹhab came to do more to offend Jehovah the God of Israel than all the kings of Israel that happened to be prior to him.

9317.label: 1 Kings 16:34
9317.text: In his days Hiʹel the Bethʹel·ite built Jerʹi·cho. At the forfeit of A·biʹram his firstborn he laid the foundation of it, and at the forfeit of Seʹgub his youngest he put up its doors, according to Jehovah’s word that he spoke by means of Joshua the son of Nun.

9318.label: 1 Kings 17:1
9318.text: And E·liʹjah the Tishʹbite from the inhabitants of Gilʹe·ad proceeded to say to Aʹhab: “As Jehovah the God of Israel before whom I do stand is living, there will occur during these years neither dew nor rain, except at the order of my word!”

9319.label: 1 Kings 17:2
9319.text: The word of Jehovah now came to him, saying:

9320.label: 1 Kings 17:3
9320.text: “Go away from here, and you must turn your way eastward and conceal yourself at the torrent valley of Cheʹrith that is east of the Jordan.

9321.label: 1 Kings 17:4
9321.text: And it must occur that from the torrent valley you should drink, and the ravens I shall certainly command to supply you food there.”

9322.label: 1 Kings 17:5
9322.text: Immediately he went and did according to the word of Jehovah, and so went and took up dwelling by the torrent valley of Cheʹrith that is east of the Jordan.

9323.label: 1 Kings 17:6
9323.text: And the ravens themselves were bringing him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and from the torrent valley he kept drinking.

9324.label: 1 Kings 17:7
9324.text: But it came about at the end of some days that the torrent valley became dry, because there had occurred no downpour upon the earth.

9325.label: 1 Kings 17:8
9325.text: The word of Jehovah now came to him, saying:

9326.label: 1 Kings 17:9
9326.text: “Rise up, go to Zarʹe·phath, which belongs to Siʹdon, and you must dwell there. Look! I shall certainly command there a woman, a widow, to supply you food.”

9327.label: 1 Kings 17:10
9327.text: Accordingly he rose up and went to Zarʹe·phath and came into the entrance of the city; and, look! a woman, a widow, was there gathering up pieces of wood. So he called to her and said: “Please, get me a sip of water in a vessel that I may drink.”

9328.label: 1 Kings 17:11
9328.text: When she began to go and get it, he went on to call to her and say: “Please, get me a bit of bread in your hand.”

9329.label: 1 Kings 17:12
9329.text: At this she said: “As Jehovah your God is living, I have no round cake, but a handful of flour in the large jar and a little oil in the small jar; and here I am gathering up a few pieces of wood, and I must go in and make something for myself and my son, and we shall have to eat it and die.”

9330.label: 1 Kings 17:13
9330.text: Then E·liʹjah said to her: “Do not be afraid. Go in, do according to your word. Only from what is there make me a small round cake first, and you must bring it out to me, and for yourself and your son you can make something afterward.

9331.label: 1 Kings 17:14
9331.text: For this is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘The large jar of flour itself will not get exhausted, and the small jar of oil itself will not fail until the day of Jehovah’s giving a downpour upon the surface of the ground.’”

9332.label: 1 Kings 17:15
9332.text: So she went and did according to E·liʹjah’s word; and she continued to eat, she together with him and her household, for days.

9333.label: 1 Kings 17:16
9333.text: The large jar of flour itself did not get exhausted, and the small jar of oil itself did not fail, according to Jehovah’s word that he had spoken by means of E·liʹjah.

9334.label: 1 Kings 17:17
9334.text: And it came about after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick, and his sickness came to be so severe that there was no breath left in him.

9335.label: 1 Kings 17:18
9335.text: At this she said to E·liʹjah: “What do I have to do with you, O man of the [true] God? You have come to me to bring my error to mind and to put my son to death.”

9336.label: 1 Kings 17:19
9336.text: But he said to her: “Give me your son.” Then he took him from her bosom and carried him up to the roof chamber, where he was dwelling, and laid him upon his own couch.

9337.label: 1 Kings 17:20
9337.text: And he began calling to Jehovah and saying: “O Jehovah my God, is it also upon the widow with whom I am residing as an alien that you must bring injury by putting her son to death?”

9338.label: 1 Kings 17:21
9338.text: And he proceeded to stretch himself upon the child three times and call to Jehovah and say: “O Jehovah my God, please, cause the soul of this child to come back within him.”

9339.label: 1 Kings 17:22
9339.text: Finally Jehovah listened to E·liʹjah’s voice, so that the soul of the child came back within him and he came to life.

9340.label: 1 Kings 17:23
9340.text: E·liʹjah now took the child and brought him down from the roof chamber into the house and gave him to his mother; and E·liʹjah then said: “See, your son is alive.”

9341.label: 1 Kings 17:24
9341.text: Upon that the woman said to E·liʹjah: “Now, indeed, I do know that you are a man of God and that Jehovah’s word in your mouth is true.”

9342.label: 1 Kings 18:1
9342.text: And it came about [after] many days that Jehovah’s own word came to E·liʹjah in the third year, saying: “Go, show yourself to Aʹhab, as I am determined to give rain upon the surface of the ground.”

9343.label: 1 Kings 18:2
9343.text: Accordingly E·liʹjah went to show himself to Aʹhab, while the famine was severe in Sa·marʹi·a.

9344.label: 1 Kings 18:3
9344.text: Meantime, Aʹhab called O·ba·diʹah, who was over the household. (Now O·ba·diʹah himself had proved to be one greatly fearing Jehovah.

9345.label: 1 Kings 18:4
9345.text: Hence it came about that when Jezʹe·bel cut off Jehovah’s prophets, O·ba·diʹah proceeded to take a hundred prophets and keep them hid by fifties in a cave, and he supplied them bread and water.)

9346.label: 1 Kings 18:5
9346.text: And Aʹhab went on to say to O·ba·diʹah: “Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the torrent valleys. Perhaps we may find green grass, that we may preserve the horses and mules alive and may not have [any more] of the beasts cut off.”

9347.label: 1 Kings 18:6
9347.text: So they divided between themselves the land through which to pass. Aʹhab himself went alone by one way, and O·ba·diʹah himself went alone by another way.

9348.label: 1 Kings 18:7
9348.text: As O·ba·diʹah continued on the way, why, there was E·liʹjah to meet him. At once he recognized him and fell upon his face and said: “Is this you, my lord E·liʹjah?”

9349.label: 1 Kings 18:8
9349.text: At this he said to him: “It is I. Go, say to your lord, ‘Here is E·liʹjah.’”

9350.label: 1 Kings 18:9
9350.text: But he said: “What sin have I committed that you should be putting your servant into the hand of Aʹhab to put me to death?

9351.label: 1 Kings 18:10
9351.text: As Jehovah your God is living, there is not a nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to look for you. After they had said, ‘He is not [here],’ he made the kingdom and the nation swear that they could not find you.

9352.label: 1 Kings 18:11
9352.text: And now you are saying, ‘Go, say to your lord: “Here is E·liʹjah.”’

9353.label: 1 Kings 18:12
9353.text: And it is bound to occur that, when I myself go from you, then the spirit of Jehovah itself will carry you away to where I shall not know; and I shall have come to tell Aʹhab, and he will not find you, and he will be bound to kill me, as your servant himself has feared Jehovah from his youth.

9354.label: 1 Kings 18:13
9354.text: Has not my lord been told what I did when Jezʹe·bel killed the prophets of Jehovah, how I kept some of the prophets of Jehovah hid, a hundred men by fifties in a cave, and kept supplying them bread and water?

9355.label: 1 Kings 18:14
9355.text: And now you are saying, ‘Go, say to your lord: “Here is E·liʹjah.”’ And he will be bound to kill me.”

9356.label: 1 Kings 18:15
9356.text: However, E·liʹjah said: “As Jehovah of armies before whom I do stand is living, today I shall show myself to him.”

9357.label: 1 Kings 18:16
9357.text: Accordingly O·ba·diʹah went off to meet Aʹhab and told him; and so Aʹhab went to meet E·liʹjah.

9358.label: 1 Kings 18:17
9358.text: And it came about that, as soon as Aʹhab saw E·liʹjah, Aʹhab immediately said to him: “Is this you, the bringer of ostracism upon Israel?”

9359.label: 1 Kings 18:18
9359.text: To this he said: “I have not brought ostracism upon Israel, but you and the house of your father have, because YOU men have left the commandments of Jehovah, and you went following the Baʹals.

9360.label: 1 Kings 18:19
9360.text: And now send, collect together all Israel to me at Mount Carʹmel and also the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baʹal and the four hundred prophets of the sacred pole, who are eating at the table of Jezʹe·bel.”

9361.label: 1 Kings 18:20
9361.text: And Aʹhab proceeded to send among all the sons of Israel and collect the prophets together at Mount Carʹmel.

9362.label: 1 Kings 18:21
9362.text: Then E·liʹjah approached all the people and said: “How long will YOU be limping upon two different opinions? If Jehovah is the [true] God, go following him; but if Baʹal is, go following him.” And the people did not say a word in answer to him.

9363.label: 1 Kings 18:22
9363.text: And E·liʹjah went on to say to the people: “I myself have been left as a prophet of Jehovah, I alone, while the prophets of Baʹal are four hundred and fifty men.

9364.label: 1 Kings 18:23
9364.text: Now let them give us two young bulls, and let them choose for themselves one young bull and cut it in pieces and put it upon the wood, but they should not put fire to it. And I myself shall dress the other young bull, and I must place it upon the wood, but I shall not put fire to it.

9365.label: 1 Kings 18:24
9365.text: And YOU must call upon the name of YOUR god, and I, for my part, shall call upon the name of Jehovah; and it must occur that the [true] God that answers by fire is the [true] God.” To this all the people answered and said: “The thing is good.”

9366.label: 1 Kings 18:25
9366.text: E·liʹjah now said to the prophets of Baʹal: “Choose for yourselves one young bull and dress it first, because YOU are the majority; and call upon the name of YOUR god, but YOU must not put fire to it.”

9367.label: 1 Kings 18:26
9367.text: Accordingly they took the young bull that he gave them. Then they dressed it, and they kept calling upon the name of Baʹal from morning till noon, saying: “O Baʹal, answer us!” But there was no voice, and there was no one answering. And they kept limping around the altar that they had made.

9368.label: 1 Kings 18:27
9368.text: And it came about at noon that E·liʹjah began to mock them and say: “Call at the top of YOUR voice, for he is a god; for he must be concerned with a matter, and he has excrement and has to go to the privy. Or maybe he is asleep and ought to wake up!”

9369.label: 1 Kings 18:28
9369.text: And they began calling at the top of their voice and cutting themselves according to their custom with daggers and with lances, until they caused blood to flow out upon them.

9370.label: 1 Kings 18:29
9370.text: And it came about that, as soon as noon was past and they continued behaving as prophets until the going up of the grain offering, there was no voice, and there was no one answering, and there was no paying of attention.

9371.label: 1 Kings 18:30
9371.text: At length E·liʹjah said to all the people: “Approach me.” So all the people approached him. Then he proceeded to mend the altar of Jehovah that was torn down.

9372.label: 1 Kings 18:31
9372.text: So E·liʹjah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom Jehovah’s word had come, saying: “Israel is what your name will become.”

9373.label: 1 Kings 18:32
9373.text: And he went on to build the stones into an altar in the name of Jehovah and to make a trench, of about the area sowed with two seah measures of seed, all around the altar.

9374.label: 1 Kings 18:33
9374.text: After that he put the pieces of wood in order and cut the young bull in pieces and placed it upon the pieces of wood. He now said: “FILL four large jars with water and pour it upon the burnt offering and upon the pieces of wood.”

9375.label: 1 Kings 18:34
9375.text: Then he said: “Do it again.” So they did it again. But he said: “Do it a third time.” So they did it a third time.

9376.label: 1 Kings 18:35
9376.text: Thus the water went all around the altar, and the trench also he filled with water.

9377.label: 1 Kings 18:36
9377.text: And it came about at the time that the grain offering goes up that E·liʹjah the prophet began to approach and say: “O Jehovah, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, today let it be known that you are God in Israel and I am your servant and it is by your word that I have done all these things.

9378.label: 1 Kings 18:37
9378.text: Answer me, O Jehovah, answer me, that this people may know that you, Jehovah, are the [true] God and you yourself have turned their heart back.”

9379.label: 1 Kings 18:38
9379.text: At that the fire of Jehovah came falling and went eating up the burnt offering and the pieces of wood and the stones and the dust, and the water that was in the trench it licked up.

9380.label: 1 Kings 18:39
9380.text: When all the people saw it, they immediately fell upon their faces and said: “Jehovah is the [true] God! Jehovah is the [true] God!”

9381.label: 1 Kings 18:40
9381.text: Then E·liʹjah said to them: “Seize the prophets of Baʹal! Do not let a single one of them escape!” At once they seized them, and E·liʹjah then brought them down to the torrent valley of Kiʹshon and slaughtered them there.

9382.label: 1 Kings 18:41
9382.text: E·liʹjah now said to Aʹhab: “Go up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of the turmoil of a downpour.”

9383.label: 1 Kings 18:42
9383.text: And Aʹhab proceeded to go up to eat and drink. As for E·liʹjah, he went up to the top of Carʹmel and began crouching to the earth and keeping his face put between his knees.

9384.label: 1 Kings 18:43
9384.text: Then he said to his attendant: “Go up, please. Look in the direction of the sea.” So he went up and looked and then said: “There is nothing at all.” And he went on to say, “Go back,” for seven times.

9385.label: 1 Kings 18:44
9385.text: And it came about at the seventh time that he got to say: “Look! There is a small cloud like a man’s palm ascending out of the sea.” He now said: “Go up, say to Aʹhab, ‘Hitch up! And go down that the downpour may not detain you!’”

9386.label: 1 Kings 18:45
9386.text: And it came about in the meantime that the heavens themselves darkened up with clouds and wind and a great downpour began to occur. And Aʹhab kept riding and made his way to Jezʹre·el.

9387.label: 1 Kings 18:46
9387.text: And the very hand of Jehovah proved to be upon E·liʹjah, so that he girded up his hips and went running ahead of Aʹhab all the way to Jezʹre·el.

9388.label: 1 Kings 19:1
9388.text: Then Aʹhab told Jezʹe·bel all that E·liʹjah had done and all about how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.

9389.label: 1 Kings 19:2
9389.text: At that Jezʹe·bel sent a messenger to E·liʹjah, saying: “So may the gods do, and so may they add to it, if at this time tomorrow I shall not make your soul like the soul of each one of them!”

9390.label: 1 Kings 19:3
9390.text: And he became afraid. Consequently he rose up and began to go for his soul and came to Beʹer-sheʹba, which belongs to Judah. Then he left his attendant behind there.

9391.label: 1 Kings 19:4
9391.text: And he himself went into the wilderness a day’s journey, and at length came and sat down under a certain broom tree. And he began to ask that his soul might die and to say: “It is enough! Now, O Jehovah, take my soul away, for I am no better than my forefathers.”

9392.label: 1 Kings 19:5
9392.text: Finally he lay down and fell asleep under the broom tree. But, look! now an angel was touching him. Then he said to him: “Rise up, eat.”

9393.label: 1 Kings 19:6
9393.text: When he looked, why, there at his head was a round cake upon heated stones and a jug of water. And he began to eat and drink, after which he lay down again.

9394.label: 1 Kings 19:7
9394.text: Later the angel of Jehovah came back a second time and touched him and said: “Rise up, eat, for the journey is too much for you.”

9395.label: 1 Kings 19:8
9395.text: So he rose up and ate and drank, and he kept going in the power of that nourishment for forty days and forty nights as far as the mountain of the [true] God, Hoʹreb.

9396.label: 1 Kings 19:9
9396.text: There he finally entered into a cave, that he might spend the night there; and, look! there was Jehovah’s word for him, and it went on to say to him: “What is your business here, E·liʹjah?”

9397.label: 1 Kings 19:10
9397.text: To this he said: “I have been absolutely jealous for Jehovah the God of armies; for the sons of Israel have left your covenant, your altars they have torn down, and your prophets they have killed with the sword, so that I only am left; and they begin looking for my soul to take it away.”

9398.label: 1 Kings 19:11
9398.text: But it said: “Go out, and you must stand on the mountain before Jehovah.” And, look! Jehovah was passing by, and a great and strong wind was rending mountains and breaking crags before Jehovah. (Jehovah was not in the wind.) And after the wind there was a quaking. (Jehovah was not in the quaking.)

9399.label: 1 Kings 19:12
9399.text: And after the quaking there was a fire. (Jehovah was not in the fire.) And after the fire there was a calm, low voice.

9400.label: 1 Kings 19:13
9400.text: And it came about that as soon as E·liʹjah heard it, he immediately wrapped his face in his official garment and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave; and, look! there was a voice for him, and it proceeded to say to him: “What is your business here, E·liʹjah?”

9401.label: 1 Kings 19:14
9401.text: To this he said: “I have been absolutely jealous for Jehovah the God of armies; for the sons of Israel have left your covenant, your altars they have torn down, and your prophets they have killed with the sword, so that I only am left; and they begin looking for my soul to take it away.”

9402.label: 1 Kings 19:15
9402.text: Jehovah now said to him: “Go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus; and you must come in and anoint Hazʹa·el as king over Syria.

9403.label: 1 Kings 19:16
9403.text: And Jeʹhu the grandson of Nimʹshi you should anoint as king over Israel; and E·liʹsha the son of Shaʹphat from Aʹbel-me·hoʹlah you should anoint as prophet in place of you.

9404.label: 1 Kings 19:17
9404.text: And it must occur that the one escaping from Hazʹa·el’s sword, Jeʹhu will put to death; and the one escaping from Jeʹhu’s sword, E·liʹsha will put to death.

9405.label: 1 Kings 19:18
9405.text: And I have let seven thousand remain in Israel, all the knees that have not bent down to Baʹal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”

9406.label: 1 Kings 19:19
9406.text: Accordingly he went from there and found E·liʹsha the son of Shaʹphat while he was plowing with twelve spans before him, and he with the twelfth. So E·liʹjah crossed over to him and threw his official garment upon him.

9407.label: 1 Kings 19:20
9407.text: At that he left the bulls and went running after E·liʹjah and said: “Let me, please, kiss my father and my mother. Then I will go following you.” At this he said to him: “Go, return; for what have I done to you?”

9408.label: 1 Kings 19:21
9408.text: So he returned from following him and then took a span of the bulls and sacrificed them, and with the implements of the bulls he boiled their flesh and then gave it to the people, and they proceeded to eat. After that he rose up and went following E·liʹjah and began to minister to him.

9409.label: 1 Kings 20:1
9409.text: As for Ben-haʹdad the king of Syria, he collected all his military forces together and also thirty-two kings with him and horses and chariots, and he proceeded to go up and lay siege to Sa·marʹi·a and fight against it.

9410.label: 1 Kings 20:2
9410.text: Then he sent messengers to Aʹhab the king of Israel at the city. And he went on to say to him: “This is what Ben-haʹdad has said,

9411.label: 1 Kings 20:3
9411.text: ‘Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your sons, the best looking, are mine.’”

9412.label: 1 Kings 20:4
9412.text: To this the king of Israel answered and said: “According to your word, my lord the king, yours I am with all that belongs to me.”

9413.label: 1 Kings 20:5
9413.text: Later the messengers came back and said: “This is what Ben-haʹdad has said, ‘I sent to you, saying: “Your silver and your gold and your wives and your sons you will give me.

9414.label: 1 Kings 20:6
9414.text: But about this time tomorrow I shall send my servants to you, and they must carefully search your house and the houses of your servants; and it must occur that everything desirable to your eyes they will put in their hand, and they must take it away.”’”

9415.label: 1 Kings 20:7
9415.text: At that the king of Israel called all the older men of the land and said: “Take note, please, and see that it is calamity that this one is seeking; for he sent to me for my wives and my sons and my silver and my gold, and I did not hold them back from him.”

9416.label: 1 Kings 20:8
9416.text: Then all the older men and all the people said to him: “Do not obey, and you should not consent.”

9417.label: 1 Kings 20:9
9417.text: So he said to the messengers of Ben-haʹdad: “Say to my lord the king, ‘All that you sent to your servant at first I shall do; but this thing I am not able to do.’” With that the messengers went off and brought word back to him.

9418.label: 1 Kings 20:10
9418.text: Ben-haʹdad now sent to him and said: “So may the gods do to me, and so may they add to it, if the dust of Sa·marʹi·a will be sufficient for handfuls for all the people that follow me!”

9419.label: 1 Kings 20:11
9419.text: In turn the king of Israel answered and said: “YOU men, speak [to him], ‘Do not let one girding on boast about himself like one unfastening.’”

9420.label: 1 Kings 20:12
9420.text: And it came about that as soon as he heard this word, while he himself and the kings were drinking in the booths, he immediately said to his servants: “Get set!” And they began to get set against the city.

9421.label: 1 Kings 20:13
9421.text: And, look! a certain prophet approached Aʹhab the king of Israel and then said: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘Have you seen all this great crowd? Here I am giving it into your hand today, and you will certainly know that I am Jehovah.’”

9422.label: 1 Kings 20:14
9422.text: Then Aʹhab said: “By whom?” to which he said: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘By the young men of the princes of the jurisdictional districts.’” Finally he said: “Who will open the battle engagement?” to which he said: “You!”

9423.label: 1 Kings 20:15
9423.text: And he proceeded to take the count of the young men of the princes of the jurisdictional districts, and they came to be two hundred and thirty-two; and after them he took the count of all the people, all the sons of Israel, seven thousand.

9424.label: 1 Kings 20:16
9424.text: And they began to go out at noon while Ben-haʹdad was drinking himself drunk in the booths, he together with the kings, the thirty-two kings that were helping him.

9425.label: 1 Kings 20:17
9425.text: When the young men of the princes of the jurisdictional districts came out first, Ben-haʹdad at once sent out; and they came telling him, saying: “There are men that have come out from Sa·marʹi·a.”

9426.label: 1 Kings 20:18
9426.text: At that he said: “Whether it is for peace that they have come out, YOU should seize them alive; or whether it is for battle that they have come out, alive is how YOU should seize them.”

9427.label: 1 Kings 20:19
9427.text: And these were the ones that came out from the city, the young men of the princes of the jurisdictional districts and the military forces that were behind them.

9428.label: 1 Kings 20:20
9428.text: And they began to strike down each one his man; and the Syrians took to flight, and Israel went in pursuit of them, but Ben-haʹdad the king of Syria got to escape upon a horse together with the horsemen.

9429.label: 1 Kings 20:21
9429.text: But the king of Israel went out and kept striking down the horses and the chariots, and he struck down the Syrians with a great slaughter.

9430.label: 1 Kings 20:22
9430.text: Later the prophet approached the king of Israel and said to him: “Go, strengthen yourself and take note and see what you are going to do; for at the return of the year the king of Syria is coming up against you.”

9431.label: 1 Kings 20:23
9431.text: As for the servants of the king of Syria, they said to him: “Their God is a God of mountains. That is why they proved stronger than we were. So, on the other hand, let us fight against them on the level land [and see] whether we shall not prove stronger than they are.

9432.label: 1 Kings 20:24
9432.text: And do this thing: Remove the kings each one from his place and put in governors instead of them.

9433.label: 1 Kings 20:25
9433.text: As for you, you should number a military force for yourself equal to the military force that fell from your side, with horse for horse and chariot for chariot; and let us fight against them on the level land [and see] whether we shall not prove stronger than they are.” Accordingly he listened to their voice and did just that way.

9434.label: 1 Kings 20:26
9434.text: And it came about at the return of the year that Ben-haʹdad proceeded to muster the Syrians and to go up to Aʹphek for battle against Israel.

9435.label: 1 Kings 20:27
9435.text: As for the sons of Israel, they were mustered and supplied and began to go out to meet them; and the sons of Israel went into camp in front of them like two tiny flocks of goats, while the Syrians, for their part, filled the earth.

9436.label: 1 Kings 20:28
9436.text: Then the man of the [true] God approached and said to the king of Israel, yes, he went on to say: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘For the reason that the Syrians have said: “Jehovah is a God of mountains, and he is not a God of low plains,” I shall have to give all this great crowd into your hand, and YOU men will certainly know that I am Jehovah.’”

9437.label: 1 Kings 20:29
9437.text: And they continued encamped for seven days, these in front of those. And it came about on the seventh day that the engagement in battle began; and the sons of Israel went striking down the Syrians, a hundred thousand men on foot in one day.

9438.label: 1 Kings 20:30
9438.text: And those that were left went fleeing to Aʹphek, to the city; and the wall came falling down upon twenty-seven thousand men that were left. As for Ben-haʹdad, he fled and finally came into the city into the innermost chamber.

9439.label: 1 Kings 20:31
9439.text: So his servants said to him: “Here, now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are kings of loving-kindness. Please, let us carry sackcloth upon our loins and ropes upon our heads, and let us go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps he will preserve your soul alive.”

9440.label: 1 Kings 20:32
9440.text: Accordingly they girded sackcloth about their loins, with ropes upon their heads, and came in to the king of Israel and said: “Your servant Ben-haʹdad has said, ‘Please, let my soul live.’” To this he said: “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”

9441.label: 1 Kings 20:33
9441.text: So the men themselves took it as an omen and quickly took it as a decision of his own accord, and they went on to say: “Ben-haʹdad is your brother.” At that he said: “Come, fetch him.” Then Ben-haʹdad went out to him; and he at once had him get up into the chariot.

9442.label: 1 Kings 20:34
9442.text: [Ben-haʹdad] now said to him: “The cities that my father took from your father I shall return; and streets you will assign to yourself in Damascus the same as my father assigned in Sa·marʹi·a.” “And as for me, in a covenant I shall send you away.” With that he concluded a covenant with him and sent him away.

9443.label: 1 Kings 20:35
9443.text: And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his friend by the word of Jehovah: “Strike me, please.” But the man refused to strike him.

9444.label: 1 Kings 20:36
9444.text: Therefore he said to him: “For the reason that you did not listen to the voice of Jehovah, here you are going away from me, and a lion will certainly strike you down.” After that he went away from beside him, and the lion got to find him and strike him down.

9445.label: 1 Kings 20:37
9445.text: And he went on to find another man and to say: “Strike me, please.” So the man struck him, striking and wounding.

9446.label: 1 Kings 20:38
9446.text: Then the prophet went and stood still for the king by the road, and he kept himself disguised with a bandage over his eyes.

9447.label: 1 Kings 20:39
9447.text: And it came about that as the king was passing by, he cried out to the king and proceeded to say: “Your servant himself went out into the thick of the battle; and, look! a man was leaving the line, and he came bringing a man to me and then said, ‘Guard this man. If he should in any way be missing, your soul will also have to take the place of his soul, or else a talent of silver you will weigh out.’

9448.label: 1 Kings 20:40
9448.text: And it came about that as your servant was active here and there, why, he himself was gone.” At this the king of Israel said to him: “Thus your own judgment is. You yourself have decided.”

9449.label: 1 Kings 20:41
9449.text: Upon that he hurriedly removed the bandage from over his eyes, and the king of Israel got to recognize him, that he was from the prophets.

9450.label: 1 Kings 20:42
9450.text: He now said to him: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘For the reason that you have let go out of your hand the man devoted to me for destruction, your soul must take the place of his soul, and your people the place of his people.’”

9451.label: 1 Kings 20:43
9451.text: At that the king of Israel went on his way toward his house, sullen and dejected, and came to Sa·marʹi·a.

9452.label: 1 Kings 21:1
9452.text: And it came about after these things that there was a vineyard that happened to belong to Naʹboth the Jezʹre·el·ite, which was in Jezʹre·el, beside the palace of Aʹhab the king of Sa·marʹi·a.

9453.label: 1 Kings 21:2
9453.text: So Aʹhab spoke to Naʹboth, saying: “Do give me your vineyard, that it may serve as a garden of vegetables to me, for it is close by my house; and let me give you in place of it a vineyard better than it. [Or] if it is good in your eyes, I will give you money as the price of this.”

9454.label: 1 Kings 21:3
9454.text: But Naʹboth said to Aʹhab: “It is unthinkable on my part, from Jehovah’s standpoint, for me to give the hereditary possession of my forefathers to you.”

9455.label: 1 Kings 21:4
9455.text: Consequently Aʹhab came into his house, sullen and dejected over the word that Naʹboth the Jezʹre·el·ite had spoken to him, when he said: “I shall not give you the hereditary possession of my forefathers.” Then he lay down upon his couch and kept his face turned, and he did not eat bread.

9456.label: 1 Kings 21:5
9456.text: Finally Jezʹe·bel his wife came in to him and spoke to him: “Why is it that your spirit is sad and you are not eating bread?”

9457.label: 1 Kings 21:6
9457.text: At that he spoke to her: “Because I proceeded to speak to Naʹboth the Jezʹre·el·ite and say to him, ‘Do give me your vineyard for money. Or, if you prefer, let me give you another vineyard in place of it.’ But he said, ‘I shall not give you my vineyard.’”

9458.label: 1 Kings 21:7
9458.text: Then Jezʹe·bel his wife said to him: “Is it you that now exercise the kingship over Israel? Rise up, eat bread and let your heart be merry. I myself shall give you the vineyard of Naʹboth the Jezʹre·el·ite.”

9459.label: 1 Kings 21:8
9459.text: Accordingly she wrote letters in Aʹhab’s name and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the older men and the nobles that were in his city dwelling with Naʹboth.

9460.label: 1 Kings 21:9
